sentence_zh: 回首往事，我意识到今天的我与五年前刚入职时的自己已大不相同。这些改变并非以戏剧性的转折点出现，而是在艰难的对话和压力之下做出的细微决定中悄然累积。成长似乎不在于突然的转变，而在于逐渐地、实质地成为一个更有耐心、更诚实的人。
mnemonic: substant 就是 substance(实质)的化身，-ial 是形容词尾巴，substantially = 拿实质说话。减肥后「实质上」瘦了20斤，不是虚晃一枪——所以它表示「大幅度地、实质性地」。记住：有实质 = 大变化。

sentence: Some of the best decisions in my life came after moments that provoked genuine reflection. A careless remark from a colleague once provoked a reaction I later regretted, yet it forced me to examine why certain words cut so deeply. Growth, it seems, often begins not with comfort but with friction—the kind that provokes us to question assumptions we had quietly accepted for years.
sentence_zh: 我人生中一些最好的决定，往往源自那些引发真正反思的时刻。同事一句无心的话曾激起我后来懊悔的反应，却也迫使我审视为什么某些话会伤得那么深。成长，似乎往往不是始于舒适，而是始于摩擦——那种促使我们质疑多年来默默接受的假设的摩擦。
mnemonic: pro（向前、往前）+ voke（喊，同 voice 的词根）→ 冲着别人「往前喊一嗓子」，把火气喊出来 = 激怒、挑衅。记住：provocation 就是那句把你「喊炸」的话。

zh: 明确的；直说的；直言不讳的
sentence: Good mentors tend to be explicit about what they expect, because vague praise leaves you guessing while clear feedback lets you grow. I once worked under a manager who never gave explicit instructions, assuming everyone could read his mind; the team drifted, deadlines slipped, and resentment quietly accumulated. Since then I have learned to ask for explicitness early, believing that a moment of directness saves weeks of misunderstanding.
sentence_zh: 好的导师往往会对自己的期望直言相告，因为模糊的夸奖让人只能瞎猜，而清晰的反馈才能让人成长。我曾有一位上司，从不给出明确的指示，以为人人都能读懂他的心思；结果团队迷失方向，交期一再拖延，不满悄然累积。从那以后我学会了尽早把话问明白，相信一次直截了当的沟通，能省去数周的误解。
mnemonic: ex（向外）+ plic（折叠）+ it → 把话向外摊开、不折叠遮掩 → explicit＝说得明明白白的。对比 implicit（im=向内，折叠在里面＝隐含的）：话摊开是explicit，折在肚子里是implicit。

sentence: For three consecutive winters I kept the same small promise to myself: write one honest page before the day began. Nothing dramatic came of it at first, but the habit quietly reshaped how I saw work and patience. Growth, I learned, rarely announces itself; it accumulates in consecutive, unglamorous days that no one applauds, until one morning the person you were has simply become the person you are.
sentence_zh: 连续三个冬天，我对自己守着同一个小小的承诺：每天开始之前写下一页诚实的文字。起初并没有什么戏剧性的收获，但这个习惯悄悄改变了我看待工作与耐心的方式。我由此明白，成长很少大张旗鼓；它沉淀在连续的、无人喝彩的平凡日子里，直到某个清晨，从前的你已悄然成为如今的你。
mnemonic: con（一起）+ secut（跟随，同sequel续集）+ ive → 一个跟着一个连在一起。想想剧追consecutive三集：一集接一集不停。记住：secut=跟，跟着走就是『连续的』。

sentence: There is a particular kind of exhaustion that comes not from hard work itself but from watching carefully laid plans come undone. When circumstances frustrate our intentions again and again, we begin to question whether persistence is wisdom or merely stubbornness. Yet I have noticed that the people who grow the most are rarely those spared such setbacks; they are the ones who treat every frustrating obstacle as evidence that the goal still matters, and who adjust their route without surrendering their direction.
sentence_zh: 有一种特别的疲惫，并非来自努力本身，而是来自眼睁睁看着精心制定的计划一再落空。当环境反复挫败我们的意图时，我们开始怀疑坚持究竟是智慧，还是仅仅固执。然而我发现，成长最多的人很少是那些幸免于挫折的人；他们往往是把每一次令人恼火的障碍都视为目标依然值得的证据，在不放弃方向的前提下调整路线。
mnemonic: frustrate 里藏着 rust（锈）：一台生了锈的机器，怎么踩油门都干转不前，人被卡得心烦。→ 生锈卡住 = 使挫败、使泄气

zh: 口齿清晰的；善于表达的；明确说出，清晰表达
collocations: 清晰地表达自己的想法
sentence: My old manager was never the loudest voice in the room, yet she was the most articulate. She could take a half-formed idea, the kind everyone senses but nobody can name, and turn it into a sentence everyone could act on. Watching her, I realized that being articulate is less about vocabulary than about clarity of thought; until you understand something yourself, no amount of eloquence will express it.
sentence_zh: 我以前的老经理从来不是房间里声音最大的人，却是最善于表达的。她能把一个半成形的想法，那种人人隐约感觉到却没人说得清的东西，变成一句人人可以照着去做的话。看着她，我明白了：善于表达靠的不是词汇量，而是思维的清晰；连自己都没弄懂的事，再多雄辩也说不明白。
mnemonic: articul 是「小关节」的词根（art 关节 + icle 小，同 article/molecule 家族）。说话像关节一样一节一节咬合到位，才叫 articulate——口齿清晰、有条理地表达。拆词有理：话有「关节」，才能说清楚。

collocations: 对这些说法持怀疑态度
sentence: I used to accept whatever promising ideas crossed my desk, but a few failed ventures left me more skeptical. These days, when a plan sounds too good to be true, I slow down and ask who benefits and what evidence exists. Skepticism, I've learned, is not cynicism; it is simply the discipline of insisting on proof before devotion.
sentence_zh: 我从前总是照单全收每一个听上去很有前景的想法，但几次失败的项目让我变得多疑起来。如今，当一份计划好得不像真的时候，我会放慢脚步，追问谁从中受益、又有什么证据。我渐渐明白，怀疑不等于愤世嫉俗；它不过是一种纪律——在倾注信任之前，先坚持要看到证据。
mnemonic: skeptical 谐音「死磕破题抠」——老板听你汇报，眉头一皱，死磕着破绽抠细节，处处挑刺：真的吗？有证据吗？这就是怀疑的态度。记住：死磕破绽=skeptical（怀疑的）。

sentence: Working in a leadership role means living under constant scrutiny. Every decision you make is examined by people whose motives you cannot always see, and at first that visibility feels unbearable. Over time, though, I learned that being watched closely can sharpen you: it forces honesty, exposes lazy habits, and teaches you to act in ways you would defend even in public.
sentence_zh: 担任领导角色意味着生活在持续的关注之下。你做出的每一个决定都会被那些动机难测的人仔细审视，起初这种无所遁形的感觉令人难以承受。但渐渐地我明白，被人密切注视其实能磨砺你：它迫使你诚实，暴露出懒散的习惯，也教会你以即使在众目睽睽下也能坦然辩护的方式行事。
mnemonic: scrutiny 谐音「死抠他你」：海关安检员对行李「死抠」，一件件翻到底。 Remember: 审查就是往死里抠细节 → 仔细检查、审查。

sentence: There is a quiet cost to suppressing what we truly feel. At first it seems like discipline, even maturity, to swallow our doubts and press on, but emotions denied do not vanish; they settle into the body, resurfacing as fatigue or resentment. Growth, I have come to believe, is less about controlling every impulse than about acknowledging it honestly, then choosing how to act.
sentence_zh: 压抑真实的感受是要付出无声代价的。起初，咽下疑虑、硬着头皮前行似乎是一种自律，甚至是一种成熟，但被否定的情绪并不会消失；它们会沉淀在身体里，最终以疲惫或怨恨的形式重新浮现。我渐渐相信，成长不在于控制每一个冲动，而在于诚实地承认它，然后再选择如何行动。
mnemonic: suppress = sup(向下) + press(压)。想象有人在你头顶往下压：向下压住情绪、新闻、 rebellion——全都按下去不让冒头。记住 press 已会 half，加个「向下」就是镇压、压制。

sentence: Growth rarely announces itself. It hides in ordinary days, waiting for us to extract meaning from what seemed like wasted time. Looking back, I can extract a quiet lesson from every failure: patience matters more than brilliance. We are, in a sense, editors of our own lives, pulling out the passages worth keeping and letting the rest dissolve.
sentence_zh: 成长很少自己宣布到来。它藏在平凡的日子里，等我们从看似虚度的时光中提炼出意义。回首往事，我能从每一次失败中汲取一个安静的教训：耐心比才华更重要。从某种意义上说，我们都是自己人生的编辑，摘出值得保存的段落，让其余的渐渐消散。
mnemonic: ex = 向外，tract = 拉（同 tractor 拖拉机、attract 吸拉）。extract 就是把里面的东西「往外拉」：拔牙、提取汁液、摘录句子，全是拉出来。记住：拉出来 = 提取。

sentence: We like to believe that loyalty is permanent, yet everyone eventually discovers how easily it can be betrayed—sometimes by others, more often by ourselves. We betray our closest friends with small omissions, betray our own convictions with quiet compromises, and each time the loss is barely visible. Perhaps growing up means learning to guard what we claim to value, so that our actions no longer contradict our words.
sentence_zh: 我们总以为忠诚是永恒的，可每个人终究会发现它是多么容易被背叛——有时是被别人，更多时候是被我们自己。我们用小小的隐瞒辜负最亲近的朋友，用悄无声息的妥协背弃自己的信念，而每一次失去都几乎难以察觉。也许成长就意味着学会守护我们口中所珍视的东西，让行动不再与言语相悖。
mnemonic: betray = be（被）+ tray（托盘）：把自己人放上托盘，端出去卖掉——被端出去，就是背叛、出卖。记忆逻辑：be「被」+ tray「端」→ 被端走 = 背叛。

zh: 官僚机构；官僚体制；官僚作风
sentence: Starting my own small business taught me more about institutions than any textbook ever did. What wears you down, I discovered, is rarely a single rejection but the slow accumulation of paperwork, waiting, and quiet refusals — the everyday texture of bureaucracy. Yet I also learned that behind every form there is usually a tired person, and that patience, politely applied, can move even the most rigid system.
sentence_zh: 自己创业让我对体制的了解超过了任何教科书。我发现，真正消磨人的从来不是某一次拒绝，而是文件、等待和无声推诿的慢慢累积——那是官僚机构日常的质感。但我也明白，每张表格背后往往站着一个疲惫的人，只要耐心并以礼相待，再僵硬的体系也能被打动。
mnemonic: bureau 本义是铺绿绒布的办公桌，后来指『局、办公机构』；cracy = 统治（如 democracy 民主）。在办公桌后面统治你 = 官僚机构。盖章、排队、踢皮球，全是 bureau 的权力。记住：办公室 + cracy 统治 = bureaucracy。

zh: 笨拙的；尴尬的；难办的；不便使用的
sentence: Growth often begins in awkward moments: the fumbled introduction at a party, the question you regret the second it leaves your mouth. We tend to treat awkwardness as a flaw to be hidden, yet it is really evidence of stretch — of attempting conversations and skills just beyond our current reach. Those who learn to sit comfortably with awkward moments usually end up moving through life with far more grace.
sentence_zh: 成长往往始于笨拙的时刻：聚会上结结巴巴的自我介绍，话一出口就后悔的问题。我们总把尴尬当作需要掩饰的缺陷，但它其实是拉伸的证明——说明我们正在尝试略微超出自身能力的对话与技能。那些学会安然面对尴尬时刻的人，最终往往能以从容优雅的姿态走完人生。
mnemonic: awkward = awk（歪、反）+ ward（朝向），字面是"朝歪的方向走"。想象你上台握手，手却伸向反方向，对方扑了个空——方向一歪，场面立刻尴尬别扭。记住：走歪了 = awkward。

sentence: It took me years to understand that an authentic life is less about grand gestures than about small, honest choices. At work, I used to perform the version of myself that others seemed to want, and it was exhausting. Gradually I learned that people trust an authentic voice, one that admits doubt and still commits. Paradoxically, the more real I became, the more freedom I found.
sentence_zh: 我花了很多年才明白，真实的生活并不在于宏大的姿态，而在于细小而诚实的选择。在工作中，我曾扮演别人希望看到的那个自己，这让人疲惫不堪。渐渐地我懂得，人们信任一种真实的声音——它承认怀疑，却依然坚定。说来矛盾，我越是真实，获得的自由反而越多。
mnemonic: authentic 里藏着 author（作者）——出自作者本人之手的才是「真迹」。博物馆看画，策展人说：这是 author 亲手 authentic（真迹），不是赝品。记住：有 author 的就是 authentic 正宗的。

sentence: Growth, I have come to believe, is less about winning arguments than about knowing when a concession costs you nothing and saves the relationship. In my first years at work I fought every point to the end, mistaking stubbornness for strength. Now I see that yielding on the small things is not weakness; it is a quiet arithmetic of what truly matters.
sentence_zh: 我渐渐相信，成长与其说在于赢得争论，不如说在于懂得什么时候一个让步不费分毫却能挽救一段关系。工作头几年，我把每个观点都争到底，误把固执当成坚强。如今我明白，在小处退让并非软弱；那是一种关于什么才真正要紧的、安静的权衡。
mnemonic: con（共同/一起）+ cess（走，同 proceed 的 cess）+ ion → 谈判时双方互相「往对方那边走一步」= 让步。记住：谈崩了，总得有人 cess 走一步，这就是 concession。

sentence: Every writer learns to live with rejection; the first few letters feel like verdicts on your worth, but over time they become something gentler, almost useful. What once read as a door slamming shut turns out to be a nudge toward a better draft, a sharper idea, a braver pitch. The fear of rejection never quite disappears, yet those who keep submitting, keep asking, keep showing up discover that it was never a wall, only a filter.
sentence_zh: 每个写作者都要学会与拒绝共处；起初的几封拒信像是给你的价值下的判决，但久而久之，它们变得温和一些，甚至有点用处。曾经读来像一扇砰然关上的门的东西，结果却成了推动你写出更好的稿子、想出更锋利的点子、做出更大胆的投稿的一次轻推。对被拒绝的恐惧从未真正消失，然而那些不断投稿、不断开口、不断出现的人会发现，那从来不是一堵墙，只是一道滤网。
mnemonic: re（往回）+ ject（扔，同 eject 弹射）→ 把东西「扔回去」→ 拒绝就是把你递来的东西丢回来。记：project 是向前扔（投出），rejection 就是往回扔回来 = 拒绝。

zh: 不足的；不胜任的；不充分的
sentence: There is a particular kind of loneliness in feeling inadequate at work, especially when everyone around you seems effortlessly competent. Yet the sensation is rarely evidence of real failure; more often it reflects the gap between what we demand of ourselves and what any human being could reasonably deliver. Learning to sit with that inadequacy, rather than frantically patching over it, may be the more honest form of growth.
sentence_zh: 在工作中感到力不从心，会带来一种独特的孤独感，尤其当你身边的人似乎都游刃有余的时候。然而这种感觉很少是真正失败的证据；它更多反映的是我们对自己的要求与任何人实际上所能做到的之间的落差。学会与这种不足共处，而不是慌乱地掩饰它，或许才是更诚实的成长方式。
mnemonic: 拆开看：in（否定）+ adequ（=equal，够、相等）+ ate。in-adequate 就是「不够量」→ 不足的、不胜任的。对比 adequate（足够的）：加了 in 就反转成不够。一句话：in 一来，够变不够。

sentence: For years I measured success by how quickly I climbed, and I climbed quickly indeed. Yet the promotions that subsequently arrived brought little of the satisfaction I had imagined; they merely raised the ceiling of my ambition. Looking back, I suspect the lesson was always there, waiting: the life you actually build matters more than the milestones you subsequently collect along the way.
sentence_zh: 多年来，我以晋升的速度来衡量成功，而且我确实升得很快。然而随后到来的那些晋升，并未带来我设想中的满足，它们只是抬高了我野心的天花板。回望过去，我怀疑那个道理一直都在，等着我去领悟：你真正经营出来的生活，远比你随后一路收集的里程碑更重要。
mnemonic: subsequently = sub(在下面) + sequ(跟随，同 sequence 顺序) + ly，字面是「跟在下面/后面地」→ 随后。记住 sequence(顺序) 里那个 sequ 就是「跟」，一个跟一个，就是后来发生。

sentence: I have come to suspect that no salary can truly compensate for the quiet erosion of a life spent doing work one barely respects. Yet we keep bargaining with ourselves, trading mornings and health for numbers on a payslip, as if the ledger would eventually balance. Perhaps maturity is realizing that meaning is never reimbursed; it must be chosen, not compensated.
sentence_zh: 我渐渐开始怀疑，任何薪水都无法真正补偿把一生耗在几乎不敬重的工作上所带来的悄然侵蚀。然而我们仍不断与自己讨价还价，用清晨和健康去换取工资单上的数字，仿佛这笔账最终会归于平衡。也许成熟就在于明白：意义从来不会得到报销，它只能被选择，而无法被补偿。
mnemonic: compensate = com(一起/补偿性) + pens(付钱、称重，同根词 pension 养老金就是『付的钱』) + ate → 该付的补着付上，就是补偿。欠了别人的，pens 一笔还回去。

sentence: In the years after graduation, I learned that most conflicts at work do not come from bad intentions but from vague expectations. A short conversation to clarify what each side actually needs can save weeks of quiet resentment. Growth, I suspect, is less about winning arguments and more about having the patience to clarify our own thinking before we ask others to understand it.
sentence_zh: 毕业后的这些年里，我明白到职场上的大多数冲突并非源于恶意，而是源于模糊的期待。一次简短的对话，澄清双方真正的需求，往往能省去数周的暗中埋怨。我猜想，成长的关键不在于赢得争论，而在于有耐心先理清自己的想法，再要求别人去理解。
mnemonic: clarify = clar(清楚的，同 clear) + ify(使动后缀)，"使变清楚"。公司开会 boss 一拍桌子：clarify!把含糊的东西变清澈。记住：clar 就是 clear 少了尾巴，-ify 一加上就"搞清楚"。

sentence: Most of what matters in life is not achieved in a single triumphant moment but through years of quiet, unglamorous striving. We strive for goals that often recede as we approach them, and yet the effort itself reshapes who we are. Perhaps the point was never to arrive, but to become someone capable of the journey.
sentence_zh: 人生中真正重要的事，大多不是在某一个辉煌瞬间完成的，而是通过多年安静而不起眼的奋斗得来的。我们为之奋斗的目标，往往在临近时又渐渐远去，然而这份努力本身重塑了我们。也许重点从来不是抵达，而是成为一个能够走完这段旅程的人。
mnemonic: strive 谐音「死拽夫」：他死命拽着丈夫往前冲，两口子为日子拼命奋斗。记住：死拽（死命拉扯）= 努力奋斗、力求。

sentence: There is a quiet way in which neglect shapes a life: not through any dramatic failure, but through the small postponements that accumulate over years. We neglect friendships because work feels urgent; we neglect our bodies because they rarely complain. Growth, though, is less about adding new habits than about noticing what we have allowed to wither, and deciding, finally, to tend to it again.
sentence_zh: 忽视有一种悄悄塑造人生的方式：不是通过什么戏剧性的失败，而是通过经年累月的小小拖延。我们 neglect 友谊，因为工作显得更紧迫；我们 neglect 身体，因为它很少抱怨。然而，成长与其说是增加新习惯，不如说是留意自己任其枯萎了什么，并最终决定重新照料它。
mnemonic: neg = 不（negative 的 neg）+ lect = 挑选（同 collect、select 里的 lect）→ 不挑不选、看都不看一眼 → 就是忽视、怠慢。想象领导说 select 你升职，结果 neg 掉了，把你 neglect 了。记：neg 否定lect 选 = 不理不选。

collocations: 一座中世纪风格的城市
sentence: Visiting the old town felt like stepping backward through centuries. The medieval walls still wrapped around the narrow streets, stubborn and gray, yet people lived inside them with quiet modern ease. It made me think about how we carry our own pasts the same way: old structures around new lives, sometimes limiting, often sheltering, always shaping what we become without ever fully announcing themselves.
sentence_zh: 走在老城里，仿佛倒退了几个世纪。中世纪的城墙依然环绕着狭窄的街道，固执而灰暗，但人们在其中过着安宁的现代生活。这让我想到，我们自己也同样背负着过去：旧的结构包裹着新的生活，有时是束缚，常常是庇护，总是在悄悄塑造着我们，却从不刻意宣示自己。
mnemonic: 拆开看：medi = 中间（如 medium 中等），ev = 时代（同 age 的词根 eva）→「中间的时代」= 古代和近代之间的年代，就是中世纪。记：medi 中间 + ev 年代 = medieval 中世纪的。

sentence: There is a quiet irony in how we measure a career: the promotions we chase, the salary figures we compare, the monetary markers of success that seem to define everything. Yet the colleagues I remember most fondly are rarely the ones who earned the most. They are the people who taught me patience, who stayed late to help, and who understood that some of life's richest returns never appear on a payslip.
sentence_zh: 我们衡量职业生涯的方式有一种安静的反讽：我们追逐的晋升、彼此比较的薪资数字，还有那些似乎能定义一切的金钱化成功标志。然而我记忆中最亲切的同事，很少是挣得最多的那些人。他们是教会我耐心的人，是留下来帮忙到深夜的人，是明白人生最丰厚的回报永远不会出现在工资单上的人。
mnemonic: monetary = money（钱）+ tary（形容词后缀，像 -ary）：钱变的形容词。钱是「money」，跟钱有关的自然就是「monetary」——monetary policy 货币政策，央行管的都是钱的事。看见 money 藏在里面，一词根永不忘。

sentence: We tend to imagine prosperity as something measured in figures—salaries, savings, the price of a house—but the word once meant something gentler: to flourish, to thrive according to one's nature. A life can look prosperous on paper while feeling strangely barren. Perhaps real prosperity is quieter than that: work that absorbs you, people who know you well, and mornings you do not dread.
sentence_zh: 我们总以为繁荣是可以用数字来衡量的东西——薪水、存款、房价——但这个词原本的含义要温和得多：蓬勃生长，按自己的天性欣欣向荣。一种人生可能在纸面上显得富足，实际上却出奇地贫瘠。也许真正的繁荣比那安静得多：有让你投入的工作，有真正了解你的人，还有你不再畏惧的清晨。
mnemonic: prosperity = pro（向前）+ sper（希望，同 spirit 同源）+ ity（名词后缀）→ 日子一直有希望往前奔 = 繁荣兴旺。记：向前 sper（希望），国家有希望就是 prosperity 繁荣。

sentence: Confidence, unlike talent, is not something we are born with; it must accumulate slowly, one small success at a time. In the early years of any career, the progress we notice daily seems negligible, yet the accumulated experience quietly reshapes how we judge, decide, and persist. Those who trust this slow deposit of effort often find, years later, that they have accumulated far more than they ever planned.
sentence_zh: 自信不同于天赋，它并非与生俱来，而是要一点一点慢慢积累，每次一小步的成功。在任何职业生涯的早期，我们每天看到的进步似乎微不足道，然而日积月累的经验却悄然改变着我们判断、决策和坚持的方式。相信这种缓慢投入的人，往往在多年之后发现，自己积累的远远超出了当初的预期。
mnemonic: accumulate = ac(不断去) + cumul(堆，同cumulus积云) + ate(动词) → 一堆一堆往上堆。天上积云就是一点点『堆』出来的，财富、知识也一样越堆越多 = 积累。记住：cumul=堆。

zh: 干预，介入；调停；介于其间
sentence: There is a quiet wisdom in knowing when to intervene and when to let things unfold. A friend in trouble does not always want rescuing; sometimes the kindest act is patient silence. Yet history teaches that staying passive can carry its own cost. In the intervening years between our mistakes and our growth, we learn that intervention, like restraint, is a matter of timing rather than intention.
sentence_zh: 知道何时干预、何时顺其自然，是一种安静智慧。陷入困境的朋友未必总想被拯救；有时最体贴的举动是耐心的沉默。然而历史告诉我们，袖手旁观也有其代价。在犯错与成长之间那段时间里，我们逐渐明白：介入与克制一样，关键在于时机，而非初衷。
mnemonic: inter（中间）+ vene（词根ven/vent=来，如 event「走出来发生的事」）→ 走到中间来 → 干预、插手。吵架时有人「走到你们中间」，就是 intervene 调停。

sentence: We often assume that character is something we declare, but in truth it is something we embody, quietly and repeatedly, in the smallest choices we make. A person may speak eloquently about integrity, yet only daily conduct embodies it. Over time, others stop listening to our words and start reading our habits, because habits are where conviction finally takes visible shape.
sentence_zh: 我们常常以为品格是可以宣讲出来的东西，但其实它是在我们最微小的选择中、安静而反复地被体现出来的。一个人也许能把正直讲得头头是道，然而唯有日常的言行才真正体现它。久而久之，别人不再听我们说什么，而是开始读我们的习惯，因为习惯才是信念最终显形的地方。
mnemonic: em（进入）+ body（身体）→ 让抽象的东西“进入身体”、获得血肉，就是“体现、具体化”。比如这句子 embody 了作者的灵魂——思想长出了身体。记住：embodiment = 有身体的东西。

sentence: We often assume that morality is fixed, handed down whole from our parents or our culture, yet living long enough teaches otherwise. Each stage of life asks a different question of us: ambition tests our honesty, comfort tests our generosity, and failure tests our compassion. What we call morality is less a rulebook than a daily negotiation with who we are becoming.
sentence_zh: 我们常常以为道德是固定不变的，是从父母或文化那里原封不动继承下来的，然而活得久了便会明白并非如此。人生的每个阶段都向我们提出不同的问题：抱负考验我们的诚实，安逸考验我们的慷慨，失败考验我们的同情心。所谓道德，与其说是一部规则手册，不如说是与我们正在成为的那种人之间的一场日常较量。
mnemonic: mor- 是拉丁词根「风俗、习惯」（如 morale 士气），-ality 是名词后缀：把社会风俗内化成行为准则，就是 morality「道德」。风俗养出的规矩 = 道德。

sentence: My grandmother was never one for grand declarations of love. She showed her affection in smaller ways: a bowl of soup left warm on the stove, an umbrella waiting by the door when the forecast looked grim. Only after she was gone did I realize how much of what I understand about caring came from watching her, quietly, over all those years.
sentence_zh: 我祖母从不善于把爱说出口。她的感情都藏在细枝末节里：炉子上温着的一碗汤，天气预报不佳时早早备在门口的伞。直到她离世后，我才意识到，我所懂得的那些关于关心的道理，大多来自这些年对她默默的观察。
mnemonic: affection = affect（感动、影响）+ ion（名词后缀）。内心被人「感动」而产生的持久情愫，就是喜爱、亲情。对比 effect 是外界的「效果」，affection 是打进心里的感动。一句话：被打动的心，才有 affection。

sentence: We all learn, sooner or later, that growing up means deciding what to conceal. As children we hid nothing, because we had nothing to lose; as adults we conceal our doubts behind confident smiles, our fatigue behind polite answers. Yet the effort of concealment is quietly exhausting. Perhaps maturity is not hiding better, but choosing, with care, which truths deserve to be shown.
sentence_zh: 我们迟早都会明白，长大就意味着决定该隐瞒什么。孩提时我们毫无遮掩，因为我们无物可失；成年后，我们把疑虑藏在自信的笑容后面，把疲惫藏在客套的回答背后。然而掩饰的代价是悄无声息的消耗。也许成熟并不是藏得更深，而是审慎地选择哪些真相值得展露。
mnemonic: con(完全) + ceal(藏) → 完全藏起来。联想 reveal(揭示)是它的反义词：re(相反)+veal=揭开。一句话：conceal 就是把东西彻底「藏」住，别人完全看不见。

sentence: We often assume that reading and writing are universal gifts, yet millions still grow up without them. Literacy shapes not only what jobs we can hold but how confidently we move through the world, how we question authority, how we tell our own stories. Watching my grandmother learn to read at sixty taught me that it is never too late to claim that power.
sentence_zh: 我们常常以为读写能力是人人皆有的天赋，然而仍有无数人在缺乏它的环境中长大。识字不仅决定了我们能胜任什么工作，还决定了我们行走于世的自信、质疑权威的勇气，以及讲述自己故事的能力。看着祖母六十岁学会认字，我明白了：掌握这份力量，永远不会太迟。
mnemonic: liter 是词根「文字、字母」（如 literature 文学、literal 字面的），-acy 是名词后缀表「性质状态」。有文字能力 = 会读会写。一句记住：literary（文学的）人才有 literacy（读写能力）。

zh: 支出；费用；（时间、精力等的）消耗
sentence: Every meaningful project demands an expenditure of more than money: time, attention, and patience are quietly drained before anything visible appears. We tend to measure cost in numbers, yet the truest expenditure is the energy we commit to something uncertain, not knowing whether it will repay us. Perhaps growth is simply learning which expenditures are worth making.
sentence_zh: 每一件有意义的事，消耗的都不只是金钱：在一切显露成效之前，时间、注意力和耐心早已被悄悄耗尽。我们习惯用数字衡量成本，然而最真实的支出，是我们投入到不确定之事上的精力——并不知道它是否会有回报。也许成长，就是学会判断哪些支出值得。
mnemonic: expenditure = ex(向外) + pend(挂/称重) + iture。古代付钱要挂秤称银子，钱'往外称出去'就是支出。对比 suspend(挂起来→暂停)同根，pend 就是'称量花钱'。一句：钱往外一称，就是花销。

sentence: There is a quiet satisfaction that comes not from titles or praise, but from competence itself — the steady knowledge that you can actually do the thing in front of you. Yet competence is never finished; each skill we master reveals another gap, and the people who grow are the ones who treat that gap not as failure, but as an invitation.
sentence_zh: 有一种安静的满足感，并非来自头衔或赞扬，而是来自胜任本身——一种踏实的确信：眼前的事，你确实做得到。然而能力永无止境；我们每掌握一项技能，便会发现另一处不足，而真正成长的人，会把这种不足看作邀请，而非失败。
mnemonic: competence = com(共同) + pet(追求、竞争，同compete竞争) + ence(名词后缀)。能跟大家同台竞争、并把事做成的本事，就是"胜任的能力"。记住：compete(竞争) competently(有能力地)——竞争得起来，说明你有能力。

sentence: There is a particular kind of loneliness in watching a friend quietly fall into distress while insisting that everything is fine. We often mistake composure for strength, and so we learn to hide what unsettles us. Yet admitting distress, even clumsily, is usually the beginning of growth rather than a confession of weakness; it opens the door that silence keeps shut.
sentence_zh: 看着朋友悄悄陷入痛苦却坚称一切安好，其中有一种特别的孤独。我们常把镇定误当作坚强，于是学会了隐藏内心的不安。然而，承认自己的痛苦——哪怕笨拙——往往是成长的开始，而非软弱的坦白；它推开了那扇被沉默紧闭的门。
mnemonic: 你已经认识 stress（压力），前面加个 dis-（加强/偏离），压力被加倍扭曲——stress 前再加一把劲，就是 stress 的加强版：distress 痛苦不堪。记住：distress = stress 的「严重版」。

sentence: Every organisation I have worked in claimed to be collaborative, yet each one quietly preserved a hierarchy that decided whose voice actually mattered. Over time I stopped resenting this and began to study it: understanding where you stand, and who genuinely holds influence, is less about flattery than about clarity. A hierarchy is not inherently cruel; it becomes so only when we mistake rank for worth.
sentence_zh: 我工作过的每一个组织都自称崇尚协作，然而每个组织都悄悄维持着一套等级制度，由它决定谁的声音真正重要。久而久之，我不再怨愤，转而开始研究它：弄清自己所处的位置、弄清谁真正有影响力，与其说是谄媚，不如说是一种清醒。等级制度本身并不残酷，只有当我们把职级误当作价值时，它才变得残酷。
mnemonic: hier 神圣 + archy 统治（如 monarchy 君主制）→ 古代祭司等级森严，像神圣的统治一样一层管一层 → 等级制度。记住：『神圣地统治』就是 hierarchy。

zh: 偏见，成见；使抱偏见；损害
sentence: Working abroad taught me how quietly prejudice operates. It rarely announces itself; it hides in assumptions we never bother to question, in the small pause before we trust someone with an unfamiliar name. Overcoming it is not a single act of tolerance but a daily discipline of listening, of admitting that our first judgments are often borrowed from people we have never met.
sentence_zh: 在国外工作让我明白偏见是如何悄无声息地运作的。它很少公开现身，而是藏在我们从未质疑过的假设里，藏在我们信任一个陌生名字之前那一瞬间的迟疑中。克服偏见并不是一次性的宽容之举，而是一种日复一日的自律：去倾听，去承认我们的第一判断往往是从素未谋面的人那里借来的。
mnemonic: 拆开看：pre（提前）+ jud（判断，同 judge）+ ice。还没了解就提前下了判断——比如没见面就说"河南人爱骗人"，这就是 prejudice 偏见。记住：判断下早了，就成了偏见。

zh: 相关联；使相互关联；相关物
sentence: I used to believe that success correlated neatly with effort, as if life kept a tidy ledger. Years of work have taught me otherwise: the variables are messier, and luck, timing, and temperament all correlate with outcomes in ways we rarely admit. Still, recognising these patterns does not excuse passivity; it simply asks us to correlate our ambitions with what we can actually control, and let the rest go.
sentence_zh: 我曾以为成功与努力之间存在着整齐的对应关系，仿佛生活记着一本清晰的账。多年的工作让我明白并非如此：变量要混乱得多，运气、时机与性情都在以我们很少承认的方式影响着结果。不过，认识到这些规律并不是消极的借口；它只是要求我们把抱负与自己真正能掌控的东西关联起来，其余的，就放手吧。
mnemonic: co（共同）+ relate（联系）→ 互相之间都有联系 = 相关。数据俩一组：一个变、另一个跟着变，就是correlate。

zh: 坚持不懈的；固执的；持续存在的
sentence: What separates those who eventually succeed from those who quietly give up is rarely talent; it is the capacity to remain persistent when progress is invisible. A persistent doubt can erode confidence over months, but a persistent effort, however small, builds something sturdier in return. Growth, I have come to believe, favours the person who shows up again the morning after everything went wrong.
sentence_zh: 最终成功的人与悄悄放弃的人之间的差别，很少在于天赋，而在于进步不可见时仍能坚持不懈。一个挥之不去的疑虑可以在数月间侵蚀信心，但一份不懈的努力，无论多么微小，反而能构筑起更坚固的东西。我渐渐相信，成长偏爱的是那个在一切出错的次日清晨依然出现的人。
mnemonic: per（贯穿到底）+ sist（站，同 stand）→ 一直站着不倒，从头站到尾 → 坚持不懈的。想想「爸爸 sister 站在那不肯走」，就是 persistent。一句话：站住不动 = 坚持。

zh: 以经验（观察）为依据的；经验主义的
sentence: We like to believe our choices are rational, but most of what we know about ourselves comes from empirical evidence gathered slowly, through trial and error. A career, a friendship, a habit of mind—each is tested against experience rather than theory. The people who grow the most are often those willing to revise their assumptions when the data of daily life contradicts them.
sentence_zh: 我们愿意相信自己的选择是理性的，但我们对自身的大部分认识，其实来自缓慢积累、通过试错获得的实证依据。一份事业、一段友谊、一种思维习惯——每一样都是靠经验而非理论来检验的。成长最快的人，往往正是那些在生活的数据与自己的假设相矛盾时，愿意修正假设的人。
mnemonic: 拆开看：em(进) + per(尝试，同 experiment 实验) + ical(形容词)。不是靠空想，而是靠'进到实验里试过'得出的——这就叫经验主义的、实证的。记逻辑：试过才有数据 = empirical。

sentence: Somewhere along the way I stopped treating caution as timidity. It is simply the discipline of looking twice before committing, of weighing what enthusiasm tends to blur. People who mistake caution for fear often rush into decisions they spend years repairing, while those who pause, ask one more question, and wait a day more rarely regret the delay.
sentence_zh: 不知从何时起，我不再把谨慎当作怯懦。它不过是一种纪律：在做决定前多看一眼，掂量那些热情往往会模糊掉的东西。把谨慎误认为恐惧的人，常常草率行事，然后用许多年去修补；而那些多停一步、多问一句、再多等一天的人，却很少为这份迟疑后悔。
mnemonic: caution 谐音「烤伤」——凑近烤炉时怕被「烤伤」，自然小心翼翼。画面：手伸向火炉前停住，心想：小心！caution 就是「小心、谨慎」。一想到「烤伤」，就提醒自己要 caution。

sentence: Most of the habits that quietly shape our lives originated in moments we barely noticed—a phrase repeated by a parent, a way of working copied from an admired colleague. Understanding where our patterns originate is uncomfortable but liberating, because once we see the source, we can ask whether the habit still serves us or merely survives out of momentum.
sentence_zh: 那些悄然塑造我们生活的习惯，大多起源于我们几乎未曾留意的瞬间——父母反复说过的一句话，或是从某位令人钦佩的同事那里学来的做事方式。弄清我们的行为模式源自何处并不轻松，却让人获得解脱，因为一旦看清了源头，我们便能追问：这个习惯如今还在滋养我们，还是仅仅凭借惯性苟延残喘？
mnemonic: originate = origin（起源，你早认识的词）+ ate（动词后缀）→ 「起源」当动词用，就是「发源、起始」。记住：认识 origin，就白捡 originate，加个 ate 而已。

zh: 值得注意的；显著的；显要人物
sentence: Looking back over a decade of quiet, unglamorous work, I realize that the moments we call notable were rarely the ones I expected. The notable figures in my life were not the loudest voices but the patient ones who stayed. Growth, it turns out, accumulates in silence, and only later does the record of it become visible enough to be called notable.
sentence_zh: 回顾十年来平静而朴素的工作，我意识到那些我们称之为“值得注意”的时刻，很少是我当初预期的。我生命中真正的显要人物并非声音最响亮的人，而是那些坚持留下的耐心之人。原来成长是在沉默中积累的，只是后来，它的痕迹才变得清晰可见，足以被称为显著。
mnemonic: notable = note（记录、注意）+ able（能…的）→ 值得被记下一笔的人或事。开会时领导说：'这事 notable，记下来！'——能被记进笔记本的，就是'值得注意的、显著的'。

sentence: Every workplace eventually confronts the moment when someone alleges misconduct against a colleague, and the word itself carries a careful weight: to allege is not to prove. Wise organizations learn to hold both truths at once — taking the claim seriously enough to investigate, yet resisting the quiet erosion of a reputation before evidence arrives.
sentence_zh: 每个职场迟早都会面对有人指控同事存在不当行为的时刻，而这个词本身就带着一种审慎的分量：指控并不等于证实。明智的组织懂得同时守住两件事——既认真对待指控、展开调查，又抵制住那种在证据到来之前就悄然侵蚀他人名誉的冲动。
mnemonic: al(朝向) + leg(法律，同 legal) → 说话时往「法律」上靠：没有真凭实据，只是往法律方向指控一下。所以 allege = 声称、指控(未经证实的)。一句话：还没定罪，只是「往法律上指」一把。

sentence: We often assume that success is a summit, a fixed point we might someday attain after years of climbing. But the people I admire most seem to treat every goal attained not as a finish line but as a doorway. What they actually attain, in the end, is not the prize itself but a steadier sense of who they are, and that quiet self-knowledge outlasts any achievement.
sentence_zh: 我们常以为成功是一座顶峰，是多年攀登后某天终能抵达的固定一点。但我最敬佩的那些人，似乎把每一个达成的目标都当作 doorway，而非终点线。到头来，他们真正获得的并不是奖赏本身，而是一种对自我更笃定的认识——而这份沉静的自知，比任何成就都更长久。
mnemonic: attain = at（去、朝向）+ tain（握住，同 contain 的 tain）→ 伸手过去握住了，才叫「达到」。想想获得目标 = obtain（ob+tain 拿到手），attain 是朝目标伸手够到它。记住：tain 就是「握」，握住了就是达成。

zh: 限制，局限；禁闭，关押；局限范围
sentence: For years she confined her ambitions to what others expected of her, working steadily but never venturing beyond the confines of her job description. Only when illness forced her to be confined to bed for a month did she begin to ask what she actually wanted. Recovery, she realized, meant not returning to old limits, but choosing her own.
sentence_zh: 多年来，她把自己的抱负局限在别人对她的期待之中，安稳地工作，却从不越出职位描述的边界。直到一场病迫使她卧床一个月，她才开始追问：自己真正想要的是什么。她意识到，康复并不意味着回到旧日的局限，而是去选择属于自己的边界。
mnemonic: con（全部）+ fin（界限，同 finish 的 fin）→ 用界限把一切圈住。想象监狱四周画满了 finish 线，谁都不能越线 → 限制、监禁。一个 fin（线）圈死你。

sentence: Most of us are raised to trust orthodox thinking, because it feels safe and comes with the approval of others. Yet growth often begins precisely where convention ends. The colleague who takes an unorthodox path may look reckless at first, but over the years his quiet willingness to question accepted practice teaches the rest of us that comfort is not the same as truth.
sentence_zh: 我们大多数人都被教导要相信正统的观念，因为它让人觉得安全，还能赢得他人的认可。然而成长往往恰恰始于常规终止之处。那个走非正统路线的同事起初看似鲁莽，但多年来，他那份默默质疑既定做法的意愿让我们其他人明白：安逸并不等于真理。
mnemonic: ortho = 正（如 orthopedic 正骨科），dox = 观点（如 paradox 悖论）→ 正统的观点 = orthodox 正统的。记忆点：观点「走对了」（dox 谐音“道”)，就是正道 = 正统。

zh: 维护，支持（原则、决定）；维持（判决）
sentence: There is something quietly admirable about people who uphold their principles even when no one is watching. Integrity is easy in the spotlight, when reputation rewards it, but far harder in the ordinary moments when compromise would cost nothing. What we uphold in private, I have come to believe, is a truer measure of character than anything we perform in public view.
sentence_zh: 那些即使无人注视也坚守自己原则的人，身上有一种安静的令人敬佩之处。在聚光灯下，当名声会奖励正直时，坚持操守很容易；但在妥协毫无代价的平凡时刻，坚持就难得多了。我渐渐相信，我们在私下里所坚守的东西，比我们在人前展现的任何表现都更能真正衡量一个人的品格。
mnemonic: up（向上）+ hold（握住）＝ 从下面向上托住 → 支撑、维护。想象裁判双手向上把奖杯 hold 住，等于维护了比赛的公正。记住：从下往上 hold 住，就是 uphold 支持、拥护。

sentence: Growth rarely announces itself in comfortable moments. It tends to arrive during hazardous stretches of life, when the ground beneath us feels uncertain and every decision carries real weight. I once resented such periods, wishing for safety, for predictability, for anything but risk. Yet looking back, I see that the people I most admire were shaped not by stability but by their willingness to endure what others feared.
sentence_zh: 成长很少在安逸的时刻悄然宣告自己。它往往出现在人生那些危险的阶段：脚下的大地飘摇不定，每个决定都举足轻重。我曾怨恨这样的时期，渴望安稳，渴望可预测，渴望一切除风险之外的东西。然而回望过去，我发现我最敬佩的那些人，并非被安稳塑造，而是被他们直面他人所惧之事的意愿所成就。
mnemonic: hazard 谐音「哈！扎的」——光脚走进废墟，大喊一声「哈！扎的！」满地碎玻璃，真危险。危险的地方，走到哪都 hazard。

zh: 补救办法；药物；赔偿；补救，纠正
sentence: Most of us reach for quick fixes when life goes wrong, but a quick fix is rarely a real remedy. The habit that caused the problem usually needs more than a pill or a weekend of rest; it needs patience and honest self-examination. In work as in health, the remedy is often slower than we would like, yet only lasting cures change who we become.
sentence_zh: 生活出问题时，我们大多数人都会寻求速效的解决办法，但速效之策很少是真正的补救之道。造成问题的那个习惯，通常不是一片药或一个周末的休息就能解决的；它需要耐心和诚实的自我审视。工作中如健康一样，补救往往比我们希望的更慢，然而唯有持久的疗效才能改变我们成为什么样的人。
mnemonic: remedy = re(重新) + med(医，同medicine) + y：药治不好就重新医一次，直到治好 → 补救、疗法。记住 med 就是「医」，remedy 就是「重新医治」＝补救。

sentence: Every meaningful project I have undertaken began the same way: not with resources, but with a problem and the stubborn need to devise some approach that might work. I have learned that the people who flourish are rarely the ones with the best training; they are the ones who, when the obvious path collapses, quietly devise another one. Creativity, it turns out, is less a gift than a habit of refusal to accept defeat.
sentence_zh: 我经历过的每一件有意义的事，开始的方式都一样：不是因为拥有资源，而是因为有一个问题，以及一种必须想出某个可行办法的执拗。我渐渐明白，走得远的人往往不是受训最出色的那些，而是当显而易见的路走不通时，能安静地再想出一条新路的人。创造力，归根结底不是天赋，而是一种拒绝认输的习惯。
mnemonic: devise = de(加强) + vis(看，同 visible) + e：认真看透了，才能想出办法。冥思苦想时反复「看」问题，突然「看」出新点子——这就是 devise「设计、想出（计划）」。记住：vis 是看，看透了才会设计。

zh: 取回；找回；检索（数据）；挽回
sentence: There is a quiet comfort in knowing that memory is not a warehouse we raid at will; we retrieve fragments, and each retrieval reshapes what we thought we kept. At work I have learned this the hard way: the file can be restored, the deadline recovered, but a colleague's trust, once frayed, is harder to retrieve. Still, retrieval is possible, and that possibility is what keeps us trying.
sentence_zh: 知道记忆并非一座随取随用的仓库，这让人心中安定几分；我们取回的是片段，而每一次取回都在重塑我们以为自己留住了的东西。工作中我吃过苦头才明白：文件可以恢复，期限可以赶上，但同事的信任一旦磨损，便更难挽回。不过挽回终究是可能的，正是这种可能让我们不断尝试。
mnemonic: re（回）+ trieve（找到，同 find 的变体）→ 找回来。球掉河里，你把球重新找回来，就是 retrieve。拆开记：一切「re」开头的词都有「回去/重新」的动作，retrieve 就是「回去取」。

sentence: There are seasons in any working life that feel like a drought: the ideas stop arriving, the effort yields little, and every morning feels drier than the last. What I have learned, slowly, is that a drought does not mean the land is dead. Beneath the surface, roots are still reaching. Creative dry spells test whether we trust the rain enough to keep planting.
sentence_zh: 任何一份工作生涯里，都有像干旱一样的季节：点子不再来临，努力收效甚微，每个清晨都比前一天更加干涸。我慢慢明白的是，干旱并不意味着土地已经死去。在表层之下，根系仍在延伸。创作的枯竭期考验的，是我们是否足够相信雨水，愿意继续播种。
mnemonic: 把 drought 拆成 dr + ought：dr 正是 dry（干）的开头，ought 意思是「应该」。本该有的水全干了——地该湿却不湿，就是旱灾。记住：dry 的开头 + 该有的没了 = drought 大旱。

zh: 令人向往的；可取的，值得拥有的
sentence: We spend much of our lives chasing what seems desirable, only to discover that the qualities we most admire in others—patience, honesty, calm—are rarely the ones we cultivate in ourselves. Perhaps growth begins when we stop asking which life is most desirable in the eyes of others and start asking which difficulties are worth carrying for our own sake.
sentence_zh: 我们一生中花了许多时间追逐那些看似令人向往的东西，却往往发现，我们最欣赏别人的那些品质——耐心、诚实、沉着——恰恰是我们自己很少培养的。也许成长的起点，在于我们不再追问哪种生活在他人眼中最为理想，而是开始追问：哪些困难，值得我们为了自己去承担。
mnemonic: desire 渴望 + able 能够 → 让人心生渴望的。可拆成「desire（欲望）+ able（…的）」，字面就是「能勾起欲望的」＝值得想要的、令人向往的。一间海景房、一份高薪工作，都是 desirable。记住：心里有 desire，它才 desirable。

zh: 忠实的；可靠的；忠贞的；信徒
sentence: Somewhere along the way, I stopped measuring friendship by its noise. The people who mattered were the quiet ones, faithful through the dull seasons when nothing dramatic happened—no crises to navigate, no triumphs to share, just ordinary weeks that could have drifted us apart. Faithfulness, I've come to believe, is not a grand gesture but a habit: showing up, remembering, staying.
sentence_zh: 不知从什么时候起，我不再用热闹与否来衡量友谊。真正重要的是那些安静的人，在平淡无事的岁月里始终忠实如一——没有危机要共渡，没有成功可分享，只有一个个本可能让彼此渐行渐远的普通星期。我渐渐相信，忠实不是壮举，而是一种习惯：出现、记得、留下。
mnemonic: faith（信念/忠诚）+ -ful（充满）＝充满信念。对朋友充满信念，就会忠诚守信：a faithful friend 忠实的朋友；对工作充满信念，就是 faithful 尽职的。记住：心里装满 faith，就是 faithful。

sentence: There is a kind of wisdom that only arrives after we have been burned once or twice. The investor who once lost everything becomes cautious, checking every figure twice before signing anything. Yet caution, taken too far, quietly hardens into fear, and we stop taking the risks that once made us feel alive. Perhaps the real skill is knowing when to be careful and when to leap.
sentence_zh: 有一种智慧，只有在我们被灼伤一两次之后才会到来。那个曾失去一切的投资者变得谨慎起来，签署任何文件前都要把每个数字核对两遍。然而，谨慎一旦过头，便悄然硬化为恐惧，我们会因此放弃那些曾让我们感到活着的冒险。也许真正的本领，在于知道何时该小心，何时该纵身一跃。
mnemonic: cautious 谐音「靠，忒慎！」——看见前方有点不对劲，心里一紧：“靠，忒（特别）慎！”于是放慢脚步，小心谨慎。谐音抓「忒慎」二字，正好就是「小心谨慎」的意思，一记就牢。

zh: 有同情心的；赞同的，支持的
collocations: 讨人喜欢（能引发共鸣）的角色
sentence: When I failed the exam for the second time, my supervisor did not scold me; instead, she listened with a sympathetic ear and reminded me that setbacks are part of any serious attempt. Her response was sympathetic without being indulgent, which is a rare balance. Looking back, I realize that what helped me grow was not comfort alone, but the sense that someone truly understood the weight of my effort.
sentence_zh: 当我第二次考试失利时，导师并没有责备我，而是带着理解倾听我，并提醒我挫折本就是任何认真尝试的一部分。她的回应充满体恤却不流于纵容，这种分寸实属难得。如今回想，我才明白真正让我成长的并非单纯的安慰，而是那种有人真正懂得我付出的沉重的感觉。
mnemonic: sym 相同 + path 感情（如 empathy 共情同根）+ etic 后缀 → 和你感情相同。朋友哭了你也眼眶发热，因为「感情相同」→ 有同情心的。记住：sym=同，path=情，同情之心。

zh: 使复苏；复兴；（使）恢复活力；重演
sentence: There are seasons in every working life when ambition quietly goes dormant. What matters is not avoiding those flat stretches but trusting that they can be revived. A single conversation with someone who still believes in the work, an afternoon spent with an old notebook of half-formed ideas, and something stirs again. We rarely resurrect our motivation by force; more often, we revive it by returning, gently, to what first drew us here.
sentence_zh: 每段职业生涯里都有一些季节，雄心会悄悄进入休眠。重要的不是回避这些平淡的时期，而是相信它们能够被重新唤醒。和某个仍然相信这份工作的人的一次交谈，一个下午翻看旧笔记本里那些未成形的想法，某种东西就再度苏醒了。我们很少能靠强求让动力起死回生；更多时候，是靠温柔地回到最初吸引我们前来的东西，让它复活。
mnemonic: re「再次」+ vive「活」(同 survive 里的 vive)→ 再活一次 = 复苏、复活。手机没电关机后重新开机「复活」，就是 revive；survive 则是一直「活下来」。记住：vive = 活，加 re 就是死而复生。

sentence: I have come to believe that hatred is rarely born in a single moment; it grows quietly, fed by small grievances we never speak aloud. In the workplace I have watched resentment harden into something darker when colleagues refuse to talk, each side collecting proofs of the other's cruelty. What dissolves hatred is usually not grand forgiveness but ordinary honesty, a conversation begun before the wounds turn permanent.
sentence_zh: 我渐渐相信，仇恨很少诞生于某个瞬间；它悄然生长，靠的是我们从不说出口的小小委屈。在职场上，我见过怨恨在同事们拒绝交流时硬化成更黑暗的东西，双方各自收集着对方残酷的证据。化解仇恨的往往不是宏大的宽恕，而是平凡坦诚的交流——在伤口变得不可挽回之前开启的那场谈话。
mnemonic: hatred = hate(恨) + red(红) → 恨得脸都red了。想象一个人气到满脸通红、咬牙切齿的样子，那种深深的恨意就是hatred。记住：恨到发红(hat+red)。

sentence: There is a kind of warmth that no heater can produce: the quiet assurance that someone has noticed you, remembered you, chosen to stay a little longer. Over the years I have learned that careers are built on competence, but lives are built on warmth — the small gestures we barely notice at the time, yet which, looking back, turn out to be the very things that carried us through.
sentence_zh: 有一种温暖是任何取暖设备都无法产生的：它是一种安静的确认，让你知道有人注意过你、记得你、愿意为你多停留片刻。这些年我渐渐明白，事业靠的是能力，而生活靠的是温情——那些当时几乎察觉不到的细微举动，回望时才发现，正是它们支撑我们走过了最难的日子。
mnemonic: warm(暖)+th(名词后缀，如 health、truth)→ 形容词变名词的温度。冬天好友递来一杯热水，掌心传来的那份 warmth。记住：warmth 比 warm 多一截，多了名词尾巴 th。

zh: 誓言，保证；抵押品；许诺，发誓
sentence: Somewhere in my thirties I stopped making grand resolutions and started keeping small pledges instead. A pledge, unlike a wish, implies that something of yours is held in trust: your time, your word, your reputation. When I told my colleagues I would finish the report by Friday, that was not a hope but a pledge, and honouring it quietly, week after week, rebuilt a trust that no speech could have restored.
sentence_zh: 三十几岁时的某个阶段，我不再许下宏大的决心，而是开始守住一个个小小的承诺。承诺与愿望不同，它意味着你的某些东西被托付了出去：你的时间、你的信誉、你的名声。当我告诉同事我会在周五之前完成报告时，那不是一种希望，而是一个承诺；一周又一周默默履行它，重建了任何漂亮话都无法挽回的信任。
mnemonic: pledge 谐音「扑雷给」：扑上去把雷都替你扛、把心都给你，这就是郑重承诺。想象宣誓时手按胸口「扑」地一声 pledge，从此说话算数——一扑一给，诺言立下。

sentence: For much of my twenties I believed that destiny was something handed to you, a script written elsewhere and merely endured. Age has softened that view. Destiny, I now think, is less a fixed verdict than a trajectory: the slow accumulation of choices, habits, and small courages that quietly point a life in one direction rather than another.
sentence_zh: 二十几岁时，我曾以为命运是别人交给你的东西，是一份写好在别处、你只能忍受的剧本。岁月让这种看法变得温和了。如今我认为，命运与其说是一道判决，不如说是一条轨迹：它由选择、习惯和一次次小小的勇气慢慢累积而成，悄无声息地把人生引向这一个方向，而非那一个。
mnemonic: destiny 谐音「得死拼」：命运不是等来的，是「得死拼」出来的。想象一个人握拳对自己喊：想改命？得死拼！一句话锁定：destiny = 得死拼才改得了的命运。

sentence: Every meaningful change I have made in my life began with something that disrupted my comfortable routine. A failed project, a sudden move, an honest conversation I had avoided for years—these disruptions felt like losses at the time, yet each one forced me to reconsider habits I had mistaken for identity. Perhaps growth is not a gentle process at all; perhaps it requires being disrupted before we can see clearly.
sentence_zh: 我人生中每一次有意义的改变，都始于某种打乱我舒适常规的事情。一次失败的项目、一次突然的搬家、一场我回避了多年的坦诚对话——这些中断在当时都像是损失，但每一次都迫使我重新审视那些我误当作自我本身的习惯。也许成长从来不是温和的过程；也许它需要先被打乱，我们才能看清一切。
mnemonic: dis（分开、打破）+ rupt（破裂，同 rupture 爆裂、interrupt 打断）→ 把完整的东西硬生生「打散震裂」，就是 disrupt。一记 rupt 就是「裂」，disrupt 就是被撕开的乱局。

zh: 使精疲力尽；用尽，耗尽；废气，排气管
sentence: There is a particular kind of tiredness that sleep cannot repair, the kind that comes when a job exhausts not only your energy but also your curiosity. I used to mistake exhaustion for dedication, wearing it like proof of seriousness. Growth, I now suspect, begins the moment we stop glorifying depletion and start asking what, exactly, is draining us.
sentence_zh: 有一种疲惫是睡眠无法修复的，那是一份工作不仅耗尽你的精力、也耗尽你的好奇心时才会有的疲倦。我曾经把筋疲力尽误当作敬业，把它像勋章一样挂在身上。如今我怀疑，成长恰恰始于我们不再美化透支、开始追问究竟是什么在消耗我们的那一刻。
mnemonic: exhaust = ex（向外）+ haust（抽、汲，同 draw water）→ 把里面的东西往外抽干：抽干水箱是耗尽资源，抽干自己就是精疲力尽。记住：haust = 抽，exhaust = 抽干耗尽。

sentence: Every meaningful choice carries some hazard, and pretending otherwise only makes us timid. I used to wait for perfect information before acting, but perfect information never comes. Now I try to weigh the risks honestly, hazard a guess when I must, and accept that failure is part of the price of growth rather than proof of foolishness.
sentence_zh: 每一个有意义的选择都带有某种风险，假装没有只会让我们变得怯懦。我从前总想等到信息万无一失再行动，可万无一失的信息从来不会出现。现在我学着诚实地掂量风险，必要时斗胆一试，并接受失败是成长的代价之一，而非愚蠢的证明。
mnemonic: hazard 谐音「哈！砸的」——楼上扔东西砸下来，多危险！站在楼下抬头一看：哈，砸的！这就是 hazard：危险、隐患。记住：听到「哈砸的」快躲开，那里有危险。

sentence: Growth rarely announces itself with trumpets; more often it is induced by quiet pressure, the accumulated friction of small failures that finally forces us to change. A mentor once induced me to take a job I thought beneath me, and the humiliation of that year taught me more than any promotion. We like to imagine we choose our turning points, but mostly they are induced by circumstance, and wisdom lies in noticing sooner.
sentence_zh: 成长很少大张旗鼓地到来；它往往是被无形的压力诱发的，是无数小挫折积累的摩擦最终迫使我们改变。一位导师曾说服我接受一份我以为配不上自己的工作，而那一年的屈辱教给我的，比任何一次升职都多。我们总以为自己选择了人生的转折点，但多数时候，转折是被环境诱发的，智慧在于更早察觉。
mnemonic: in（进入）+duce（引导，同conduct的duc）→ 往里引导 → 诱导、引起。想象用一根吸管（duce像吸管）把人往里引导，诱导他进圈套：广告induce你想买。

zh: 指定，任命；指明；已受任而未就职的
sentence: When our team lost its lead, no one was formally designated to take over, and for weeks decisions drifted. What I learned from that period is that ambiguity is rarely neutral: without someone clearly designated as responsible, responsibility quietly dissolves. Now, whenever a group I belong to stalls, I ask who, exactly, has been designated to decide.
sentence_zh: 当我们团队失去了负责人，没有人被正式指定接任，几周以来决策一直悬而未决。我从那段时期学到的是，模糊很少是中立的：如果没有明确指定谁来负责，责任就会悄然消散。如今，每当我所在的团队陷入停滞，我都会追问：究竟指定了谁来拍板。
mnemonic: de（强调）+ sign（记号）+ ate（动词后缀）→ 在某物上做出记号并指明：指定、任命。老板在新办公桌上sign（画个记号），ate掉候选名单——「做记号」就是 designate 指定。

sentence: We like to believe that growth follows a plan, as if someone could prescribe the exact steps to becoming wiser or kinder. But life rarely cooperates with such tidy instructions. What a doctor prescribes for the body, no mentor can prescribe for the soul; we each discover our remedies slowly, through failure, patience, and the quiet honesty of ordinary days.
sentence_zh: 我们总喜欢相信成长有一条既定的路线，仿佛有人能开出通往智慧与善良的精确步骤。但生活很少配合这些整齐的说明书。医生能为身体开的药方，却没有导师能为心灵开出处方；我们各自在失败、耐心和平凡日子里安静的诚实之中，慢慢找到自己的解药。
mnemonic: pre（提前）+ scribe（写，同 script 手稿）：医生提前把药方写好 → 开处方。引申为「规定、指定」。scribe 就是写字的人，如 describe（写下来＝描述）。记：开处方就是提前写好字。

sentence: In the early years of my career, I mistook efficiency for excellence and treated courtesy as a needless ornament. It took a patient mentor, who answered every junior question out of courtesy rather than obligation, to show me otherwise. Small gestures—a returned email, a genuine thank-you—cost almost nothing, yet they build the quiet trust that no cleverness or speed can buy back once lost.
sentence_zh: 职业生涯早期，我把高效等同于出色，把礼貌当作多余的点缀。直到一位耐心的导师出现——他回答每个初级问题都是出于礼貌而非义务——我才明白过来。小小的举动——一封及时回复的邮件、一句真诚的感谢——几乎不费什么力气，却能建立起一种安静的信任；这种信任一旦失去，再多的聪明和速度也买不回来。
mnemonic: courtesy = court（宫廷）+ esy。古时在宫廷里说话行事要讲规矩、懂分寸，宫廷式的举止就是有礼有节。记住：在court（宫廷）里行事，处处显礼貌——这就是礼节、谦恭。

sentence: There was a time when I measured a good year by output—more projects, more hours, more things finished. Now I think of a good life more like circulation: ideas must move between people, money must flow honestly, and rest must return to the body. Whatever stops moving, I've learned, quietly stops being alive.
sentence_zh: 曾经我用产出来衡量一个好年份——更多的项目、更多的时间、更多完成的事。如今我把好的生活想成一种循环：想法要在人与人之间流动，金钱要诚实地流转，休息要回归身体。我渐渐明白，凡是停止流动的东西，都在悄然失去生命力。
mnemonic: circ（圆圈，同 circle）+ ul + ate（动词）→ 绕着圈走 = 循环。记住 circle「圆」这个家族词，blood circulation 就是血液绕着身体转圈跑。一句话：绕圈圈的，就是循环。

sentence: Growth, in life as in markets, is rarely a smooth line; it tends to arrive in explosive bursts after long stretches of quiet, unglamorous effort. The same is true of people. Someone with an explosive temper may, beneath the noise, carry a decade of unspoken frustration, and understanding that changes how we judge the outburst.
sentence_zh: 成长，如同市场，很少是一条平滑的曲线；它往往在长期安静而不起眼的努力之后，以爆炸式的方式突然到来。人也一样。脾气火爆的人，在喧嚣之下，可能积压着十年未曾说出的委屈，明白这一点，便会改变我们看待爆发的方式。
mnemonic: explosive = ex（向外）+ plos（爆炸、炸裂，同 explode）+ ive（形容词后缀）。想想 explode（爆炸）你已认识，它的东西就是「爆炸性的」：新闻爆点、脾气火爆都能用它。一句话：能 explode 的，就是 explosive。

sentence: Growth rarely announces itself loudly; more often it arrives when a single conversation illuminates something we had stumbled past for years. A good mentor does not hand us answers but illuminates the questions themselves, so that what once seemed like fog becomes a landscape we can navigate. Perhaps that is the quiet gift of understanding: not certainty, but clearer sight.
sentence_zh: 成长很少大张旗鼓地到来；更多时候，它出现在某一次谈话突然照亮了我们多年视而不见的东西的时候。好的导师不会直接给我们答案，而是照亮问题本身，让曾经的迷雾变成一片可以行走的风景。也许这就是理解的安静馈赠：不是确定性，而是更清晰的视野。
mnemonic: illuminate 拆成 il(=in,向内/加强) + lumin(光，如 luminous 发光的) + ate 动词后缀 → 往里面灌光。想想台灯一开，黑屋里的书页瞬间被「灌满光」= 照亮；比喻义是让脑子也开灯 = 阐明、启发。记住 lumin 就是「光」这个根，一灯全亮。

zh: 穿透；渗透；看穿，洞察；打入
sentence: Some ideas move slowly at first, knocking politely at the door of our attention, while others penetrate almost at once, changing how we see everything afterwards. Real understanding works this way too: it rarely arrives through loud argument, but seeps quietly into the mind until one morning we realize a conviction has settled there, deep enough that no passing doubt can dislodge it.
sentence_zh: 有些观念起初来得很慢，礼貌地敲着我们注意力的大门；而另一些观念几乎瞬间就穿透进来，从此改变了我们看待一切的方式。真正的理解也是如此：它很少借助高声的辩论抵达，而是悄然渗入头脑，直到某个清晨我们才发觉，一种信念已在心中扎根，深到任何转瞬即逝的疑虑都无法撼动它。
mnemonic: pen（钢笔尖）+ eat（吃进去）→ 笔尖把纸“吃”穿一个洞：用笔尖狠狠一戳，把纸穿透。penetrate 就是“刺穿、渗透”。一句记住：笔尖吃透纸面。

sentence: There is a quiet strength in optimism, though we often mistake it for naivety. Real optimism is not the refusal to see problems; it is the conviction that effort can still bend outcomes toward something better. In work, as in life, the person who keeps a thread of optimism through setbacks tends to try one more time, and that one extra attempt is often where everything turns.
sentence_zh: 乐观之中蕴藏着一种安静的力量，尽管我们常把它误认为天真。真正的乐观并不是拒绝看见问题，而是相信努力仍能把结果扭向更好的方向。无论在工作中还是生活里，那个在挫折中依然保留一丝乐观的人往往会再多试一次，而这一次额外的尝试，往往正是转机所在。
mnemonic: optimism = optim（最佳，同 optimum 最优值）+ ism（主义）。永远相信『最优解』会出现，就是乐观主义。看到 optim- 就想到『总往最好的想』。

sentence: Growth rarely comes from bursts of inspiration; it comes from the quiet, unglamorous work of showing up in a systematic way. When I finally stopped relying on willpower and built a routine instead—same hour, same desk, same small goals—progress stopped feeling like luck. What looked like talent in others, I began to suspect, was often just systematic effort wearing a more attractive face.
sentence_zh: 成长很少来自灵感的迸发，而是来自那种安静、不起眼的、以系统化方式日复一日的坚持。当我终于不再依赖意志力，而是建立起一套常规——同一时间、同一书桌、同样的小目标——进步便不再像运气。我开始怀疑，别人身上看似天赋的东西，往往只是披着更体面外衣的系统性努力。
mnemonic: system（系统）+ atic（形容词后缀）→ 像系统一样的。想象把杂乱的文件按文件夹一层层归好：不是随手乱放，而是像系统一样分门别类。有系统 = 有条理的、系统化的。记住：systematic 就是 system 长出的形容词尾巴。

sentence: In the years after I changed careers, doubt became a near-daily visitor, and I learned that no one else could truly reassure me for long. Friends offered kind words, yet their reassurance faded by morning. What lasted was quieter: small evidence, gathered patiently, that the work itself was growing in my hands. Confidence, it turns out, is not something we receive but something we slowly build and keep.
sentence_zh: 在我转行之后的那些年里，怀疑几乎成了每日的访客，我渐渐明白，没有人能长久地真正让我安心。朋友们说些宽慰的话，可那份安心到了清晨便消散了。真正留存下来的是更安静的东西：那些耐心积累起来的小小证据，证明这份工作正在我手中慢慢生长。原来，自信不是别人给予的，而是我们一点点建立并守护的。
mnemonic: re + assure：assure 本身就是「保证」，re 表示「再一次」。别人慌了，你再说一遍「保证没事」——reassure 就是打消疑虑、再保证一次。一遍不够？那就 reassure。

zh: 符合，一致；相当，类似；通信
sentence: For years I kept a pen pal from university, and even after our careers pulled us across continents, we still corresponded a few times each season. Rereading her letters, I notice how our ideas of success no longer correspond to the ambitions we once shared. Growth, it seems, is measured in the quiet distance between who we were and who we write as now.
sentence_zh: 多年来我一直与一位大学时的笔友保持联系，即便各自的事业把我们带往不同的大陆，我们仍会每季通几次信。重读她的来信，我发现我们对成功的理解已不再对应曾经共同的抱负。成长，或许正是以我们过去的样子与如今落笔的自己之间那段安静的距离来衡量的。
mnemonic: 拆开看：cor（=com，共同）+ respond（回应）。两人共同回应对方——你写一句我回一句，就是「通信」；你说的和我查的对上了，就是「相符」。记住：互相 respond = correspond。

sentence: Growth often feels less like acquiring new things and more like deciding what to discard. We carry assumptions gathered in childhood, strategies that once protected us, ambitions borrowed from other people's dreams. Maturity, perhaps, is the slow courage of discarding what no longer serves us—not with bitterness, but with the quiet gratitude of someone finally clearing a crowded room to let the light in.
sentence_zh: 成长常常不像获得新事物，更像决定该丢弃什么。我们背负着童年积累的假设、曾经保护过我们的策略、从别人的梦想里借来的抱负。成熟也许就是一种缓慢的勇气：摒弃那些不再于我们有用的东西——不是带着怨怼，而是带着一种静静的感激，仿佛终于清理了拥挤的房间，好让光进来。
mnemonic: dis(离开) + card(牌)：打牌时抓到烂牌就甩出去——把牌“发走”就是扔掉。discard = 丢弃、抛弃。记法：不要的牌，discard！

sentence: There is a quiet strength in restraint, one that becomes visible only when tempers flare around you and you choose not to add fuel to the fire. In my early years at work, I mistook restraint for weakness, believing that speaking loudest meant winning. Now I understand that holding back a sharp remark often does more good than any clever argument, giving others room to think, and giving myself room to grow.
sentence_zh: 克制之中蕴藏着一种安静的力量，只有当周围的人怒火中烧而你选择不再火上浇油时，这种力量才会显现。工作初期，我曾误把克制当作软弱，以为嗓门最大的人就是赢家。如今我才明白，忍住一句刻薄的话，往往比任何机智的争辩都更有益——它给别人留下思考的空间，也给自己留出成长的空间。
mnemonic: restraint = re(往回) + strain(拉紧，同 strain 拉伤)。马被缰绳往回勒紧，就是被「拉住不放」→ 克制、约束。所谓 restraint，就是心里那根把你往回拉紧的绳子。

sentence: In my twenties I treated every interview as a performance for a prospective employer, rehearsing answers until they lost all meaning. Only later did I realize that the questions worth asking run the other way: not whether they would hire me, but whether the life this job promised was one I actually wanted. The word prospective, after all, describes something imagined, and imagination is rarely as honest as experience.
sentence_zh: 二十几岁时，我把每次面试都当成给未来雇主的一场表演，反复排练答案，直到它们失去所有意义。很久之后我才明白，值得追问的问题其实方向相反：不是他们会不会录用我，而是这份工作所许诺的生活，是否真的是我想要的。毕竟 prospective 这个词描述的是想象中的东西，而想象往往不如亲身经历来得诚实。
mnemonic: pro（向前）+ spect（看）+ ive → 向前看的：客户还没来就先盯着，这些就是「潜在的、未来的」客户 prospective customers。记住 spect 就是 inspect（检查）里的「看」。

sentence: We often mistake abundance for having more things, yet the richest lives I have observed were built on an abundance of time, attention, and friendship rather than possessions. When someone approaches work with a sense of abundance, they share credit freely and help colleagues without keeping score. Scarcity narrows the mind; abundance widens it, making room for generosity, patience, and the quiet confidence that there is enough to go around.
sentence_zh: 我们常把富足误认为拥有更多东西，然而我见过的最丰盈的人生，靠的并不是财物，而是充裕的时间、专注与友谊。当一个人怀着富足感去工作时，他们会慷慨地分享功劳，帮助同事而不计较得失。匮乏让思维变得狭隘；富足则让心胸开阔，为慷慨、耐心，以及一种“资源足够大家分享”的从容自信留出空间。
mnemonic: abundance 读作「阿蹦到死」？不如记 a bun dance：a bun（一个面包）+ dance（跳舞）——面包多到会跳舞，说明粮食满仓、富足有余。谐音「阿，蹦到（钱堆里）」，一睁眼全是钞票 = 大量、丰裕。

sentence: There were moments in my twenties when I came close to despair, convinced that every door had closed while others walked through theirs with ease. What saved me, I think, was realizing that despair is rarely a verdict on life itself; it is a signal that we have been staring too long at one closed window. Time, patience, and a small change of direction can quietly restore hope.
sentence_zh: 二十几岁的时候，我有好几次几乎陷入绝望，以为所有的门都已关上，而别人却轻而易举地走进了属于自己的那扇。后来拯救我的，大概是明白了绝望很少是对生活本身的判决，它只是一个信号，说明我们盯着那扇关上的窗看得太久了。时间、耐心，加上一点方向上的改变，便能悄悄地唤回希望。
mnemonic: despair = de(去掉) + spair(谐音「思盼」，希望)。没了思盼，希望被剥掉 → 绝望。对比 desire(渴望)还有盼头，despair 连盼都盼不动了。记住：去掉了 spair（思盼）＝绝望。

sentence: By thirty, I had learned to treat every tempting offer as a proposition to be examined rather than a gift to be accepted. Some propositions wear the language of opportunity; others merely borrow it. The discipline of asking what someone truly gains from my agreement has saved me more regret than any talent, and taught me that skepticism, politely held, is a form of self-respect.
sentence_zh: 到了三十岁，我学会了把每个诱人的提议当作有待审视的命题，而不是等待接受的礼物。有些提议披着机遇的语言，另一些只是借用了它。追问对方究竟能从我的同意中得到什么，这一习惯为我省下的遗憾胜过任何才能，也让我懂得：温和持有的怀疑，是一种自尊。
mnemonic: pro（向前）+ posit（放，同 position「摆放」）→ 把想法「摆到面前」给别人看 = 提议、主张；数学里摆出来的论断就是「命题」。记：像 position 一样 posit，往前一放就是 proposition。

zh: 履行；实现；满足（需求、期望）
sentence: There is a quiet difference between a life that merely runs on schedule and one that feels genuinely fulfilling. We spend years chasing deadlines, yet the moments we remember are those where we fulfilled a promise to someone, or finally met a standard we had set for ourselves. Perhaps fulfillment is less about reaching goals than about honoring them.
sentence_zh: 一种只是按部就班运转的人生，和一种真正充实的人生之间，存在着微妙的差别。我们花多年追逐各种截止期限，可真正记得住的，却是那些履行了对某人的承诺、或终于达到自己定下的标准的时刻。也许满足感与其说在于达成目标，不如说在于坚守目标。
mnemonic: fulfill = full（满）+ fill（装满）→ 装得满满的 → 任务填满了、心愿装满了，就是「完成、实现」。想象一个水桶被完全装满，fulfill 的那一刻，承诺兑现了。一句话：装满即达成。

sentence: Growing older has taught me that a person can hold two opposing truths at once without being dishonest. The manager who preaches balance yet answers emails at midnight lives a quiet contradiction, and perhaps we all do. Rather than smoothing every inconsistency away, maturity may mean learning to sit with these tensions, noticing where our stated values and actual choices diverge, and slowly narrowing that gap.
sentence_zh: 年龄渐长让我明白，一个人可以同时持有两种相反的真相，而这并不等于虚伪。那位宣扬工作与生活平衡、却在午夜回复邮件的经理，正过着一种无声的矛盾——也许我们都如此。成熟或许不是抹平每一处不一致，而是学会与这些张力共处，察觉我们宣称的价值观与实际选择之间的落差，并慢慢缩小这道鸿沟。
mnemonic: contra（相反）+ dict（说，如 dictionary 词典）→ 对着说反话 → 矛盾。老师刚说'对'，你偏说'不对'，这就是 contradiction。记住：dict 是'说'，contra 是'反着'。

sentence: By middle age, most of us have watched some cherished assumption shatter — the belief that hard work guarantees reward, or that the people we love will always stay. What matters is not the shattering itself but what we do with the fragments: whether we sweep them aside in bitterness, or slowly gather them into something humbler and more durable than what stood before.
sentence_zh: 人到中年，我们大多都目睹过某种珍视的信念被击碎——比如相信努力必有回报，或者所爱的人会永远留在身边。重要的不是破碎本身，而是我们如何对待那些碎片：是怀着苦涩将它们扫到一边，还是慢慢把它们拾起，拼成某种比从前更谦逊、也更坚固的东西。
mnemonic: shatter 谐音『摔特』——东西摔到地上摔得特别碎。玻璃杯『摔特』一声，碎了一地，就是 shatter：打碎、粉碎。记住：一摔就特碎！

sentence: Growth rarely announces itself gently; more often it arrives to startle us out of routines we mistook for comfort. I was startled, last autumn, by how quickly a decade of careful habits had hardened into a cage of my own making. What unsettles us is not always harm—sometimes it is the sudden evidence that we are still capable of change.
sentence_zh: 成长很少温和地宣告自己的到来；它往往突然降临，把我们从那些误以为是安逸的惯例中惊醒。去年秋天，我吃惊地发现，十年间小心翼翼养成的习惯，竟如此之快地凝固成了自己亲手打造的牢笼。让我们不安的并不总是伤害——有时恰恰是那突如其来的证据，证明我们依然有能力改变。
mnemonic: startle = start（起步）+ le（拼音“了”）：猫刚 start 要跑，你脚下突然“了”一声——吓一跳！被吓的瞬间就是动作刚要开始那一下，start 一动你就 startle。记住：start 一起步就被“了”一下 = 惊吓。

zh: 华丽的；极好的；非常漂亮的
sentence: There is a quiet kind of joy in noticing what we usually hurry past. Yesterday evening I stepped outside and found the sky absolutely gorgeous, streaked with orange and violet above the rooftops. It lasted perhaps ten minutes, and most people missed it entirely, absorbed in screens and errands. Perhaps growth means training ourselves to pause, because beauty is always offering itself, free of charge, to anyone willing to look up.
sentence_zh: 在留意那些我们通常匆匆错过的事物之中，藏着一种安静的喜悦。昨天傍晚我走到屋外，发现天空美得惊人，橙色与紫色在屋顶上空交织。它大概只持续了十分钟，而大多数人完全错过了，埋头于屏幕和琐事之中。也许成长就意味着训练自己停下来，因为美总在无偿地呈现自己，只要有人愿意抬头去看。
mnemonic: gorge（峡谷）+ ous → 美得像科罗拉多大峡谷一样壮丽夺目。想想站在峡谷边看日出的震撼感：gorgeous！记住：美到像大峡谷 = 华丽极了。

sentence: There is a kind of mastery that comes only from years of working with precision. A surgeon, a watchmaker, a careful writer — all of them understand that small errors compound quietly until they become failures. What looks like talent from the outside is often just precision practiced until it becomes invisible, a discipline so deeply absorbed that even hesitation disappears into the craft itself.
sentence_zh: 有一种精通，只有经过多年精准的打磨才能获得。外科医生、钟表匠、严谨的作家——他们都明白，微小的错误会悄然累积，最终酿成失败。在外人看来像是天赋的东西，往往不过是把精准练习到浑然不觉的程度，一种被深深吸收的纪律，连犹豫本身都消失在技艺之中。
mnemonic: precision = pre（预先）+ cis（切，如 scissors）+ ion。像裁缝下剪刀前先量好尺寸，一刀下去分毫不差——预先算好再切，才切得精准。pre+切 = 精确。

sentence: Somewhere along the way, I stopped measuring my life by grand outcomes and began noticing what was quietly around me: a magnificent sunset after an ordinary day of work, the patience of a friend who never asked for anything in return. Growth, it turns out, is less about chasing the spectacular and more about recognizing the magnificent things already folded into our routines.
sentence_zh: 不知从什么时候起，我不再用宏大的成果来衡量自己的人生，而是开始留意身边安静的事物：平凡工作一天之后那场壮丽的日落，从不求回报的朋友的耐心。原来，成长与其说是追逐那些惊人的时刻，不如说是学会辨认那些早已融入日常的、了不起的东西。
mnemonic: magnificent = magn（大，同 magic 里的 magn?）不对——记 magn=大（如 magnitude 大小）+ fic（做）+ ent（形容词）：『做得很大』→ 宏伟壮丽。想想紫禁城：大规制做成，自然 magnificent。

sentence: Everyone carries something peculiar: a way of pausing before speaking, a superstition never explained. At first such quirks seem like flaws to be corrected, but over the years I have come to see them as signatures. What is peculiar to a person is often what makes them irreplaceable, and learning to accept my own oddities has been quieter, harder work than any ambition.
sentence_zh: 每个人都带着某种奇特之处：说话前特有的停顿，一个从未解释过的小迷信。起初这些怪癖像是需要纠正的缺点，但这些年我渐渐明白，它们其实是一个人的签名。属于某人独有的东西，往往正是让他无可替代的原因；而学会接纳自己的古怪，比任何雄心都更安静，也更艰难。
mnemonic: peculiar 谐音「皮裤里儿」：有人反穿皮裤还露个里儿，路人纷纷侧目——太古怪了！他就是个「皮裤里儿」怪人。所以 peculiar = 古怪的、独特的。记住：穿皮裤露里儿的人最peculiar。

sentence: I have come to believe that being enthusiastic is less a temperament than a discipline. The people I most admire at work are not the naturally brightest, but those who greet each messy, uncertain project with genuine energy. Enthusiasm, it turns out, is contagious: it steadies a team when results are slow, and it persuades others that the effort is worth making long before success is guaranteed.
sentence_zh: 我渐渐相信，充满热情与其说是一种天性，不如说是一种修炼。我在工作中最敬佩的人，并非天资最出众的那一批，而是那些以真诚的干劲迎接每个混乱而充满不确定性的项目的人。热情原来是有感染力的：当成果迟迟不来时，它能让团队保持镇定，并在成功尚无保证之时，就让人相信这份努力是值得的。
mnemonic: en（进入）+ thus（希腊神thuos，献祭神灵时狂热兴奋）+ iastic → 进入神灵附体的状态 = 热情洋溢的。想象被神附身后手舞足蹈，这就是enthusiastic的状态。

sentence: For years I treated work as my salvation, believing that enough effort could rescue me from every doubt. But salvation rarely arrives the way we expect; it came instead from admitting weakness, from letting others see the unfinished version of myself. Growth, I now think, is less about saving ourselves single-handedly and more about allowing ourselves to be found.
sentence_zh: 多年来我把工作当作救赎，以为足够努力就能将我从一切疑虑中解救出来。但救赎很少以我们期待的方式到来；它反而来自承认脆弱，来自让别人看见那个尚未完成的自己。如今我想，成长与其说是一手拯救自己，不如说是允许自己被人找到。
mnemonic: salvation = salv(救，同 save 的近亲，如 salvage 打捞) + ation(名词后缀) → 被救的行为 = 拯救。记：salv 就是 save 换了件马甲，见到它就想到「救」。

collocations: 有一个人，也就是我的导师
sentence: Looking back on the years I spent chasing every opportunity, I realize that progress came from restraint, namely the discipline to say no to good things in order to say yes to great ones. Most of us do not lack ambition; what we lack is a filter. Growth, it turns out, is less about adding and more about choosing, namely choosing the two or three commitments worth our whole heart.
sentence_zh: 回想那些年我追逐每一个机会的日子，我意识到进步其实源于克制，也就是这样一种自律：对好事说不，才能对更好的事说是。我们大多数人并不缺雄心，缺的是一个过滤器。成长原来不在于不断添加，而在于选择——即选出那两三件值得我们全心投入的事。
mnemonic: 拆开看：name 名字 + ly → 「叫出名字」。老师点名时一个个叫名字，被叫到的就是具体指的那个人，所以 namely = 也就是、即——把笼统的话落到具体名字上。记：点名， namely 点到谁就是谁。

sentence: Talent, however real, rarely survives on its own; it needs someone to nurture it through the indifferent early years, when effort seems to return nothing. A mentor who believes quietly, a parent who withholds judgment, a friend who listens—these are the conditions in which ambition takes root. We often credit the flower while forgetting the patient, unglamorous work of nurturing the soil it grew from.
sentence_zh: 天赋再真实，也很难独自存活；它需要有人在自己 seemingly 毫无回报的最初岁月里去滋养它。一位默默相信你的导师，一位不轻易评判的父母，一位愿意倾听的朋友——正是这些条件让抱负得以扎根。我们常常只赞美花朵，却忘记了培育它脚下那片土壤的、耐心而不起眼的功课。
mnemonic: nurture 谐音「嫩土」：幼苗要长得好，得种在嫩土里，天天浇水施肥、精心培育——这就是 nurture「养育、培养」。记忆逻辑：嫩土养苗 = 养育培养。

sentence: There was a time when any setback at work could leave me furious, as if the world had singled me out for injustice. With age I have learned that anger, however justified, rarely improves the situation; it only narrows the mind. What once made me furious now makes me curious, and that quiet shift has mattered more than any promotion ever did.
sentence_zh: 曾经，工作中任何一点挫折都能让我勃然大怒，仿佛全世界都在故意与我作对。随着年龄增长，我渐渐明白，愤怒无论多么有理，都很少能改善局面，只会让心胸变得狭窄。从前让我暴怒的事，如今只会让我好奇，而这份安静的转变，比任何一次升职都更有意义。
mnemonic: furious 谐音「发热累死」——气得浑身发热、气到累死，就是暴怒。怒火攻心时人不就是这样吗？记住：气到「发热累死」＝狂怒的。

collocations: it is undoubtedly the case that
sentence: Looking back on the years I spent learning to write, I can see that failure undoubtedly shaped me more than success ever did. Every rejected draft forced me to reconsider what I actually meant to say, and every harsh comment, however painful, sharpened my judgment. Growth rarely feels like progress while it is happening; it is undoubtedly only in retrospect that the struggle reveals its purpose.
sentence_zh: 回顾我学习写作的那些年，我发现失败无疑比成功更能塑造我。每一份被拒绝的草稿都迫使我重新思考自己真正想说什么，每一条尖锐的评论，无论多么刺痛，都磨砺了我的判断力。成长在发生时很少让人感觉像是进步；无疑只有回首时，挣扎才会显露出它的意义。
mnemonic: un不 + doubt怀疑 + ed形容词尾 → 不带怀疑的 → 毫无疑问地。Doubt本身谐音「打不」：想打都打不破的证据，当然毫无疑问。记住 doubt=怀疑，undoubtedly就是板上钉钉。

zh: 痴迷；萦绕心头的执念；强迫观念
sentence: There is a fine line between passion and obsession, and most of us cross it without noticing. What begins as genuine curiosity about our work can slowly harden into an obsession with results, until we no longer enjoy the process itself. I have learned to watch for that shift: the moment when a dream stops expanding your life and starts shrinking it, quietly taking everything else with it.
sentence_zh: 热情与痴迷之间只有一线之隔，而我们大多数人在不知不觉中就越过了那条线。对工作的真正好奇，会慢慢硬化成对结果的执念，直到我们再也享受不到过程本身的乐趣。我学会了留意这种转变：就在梦想不再拓宽你的生活、反而开始让它萎缩的那一刻，它悄悄地捎走了其余的一切。
mnemonic: ob（对着）+ sess（坐，同 sit 系）+ ion → 整天「对着坐」死守不放：恋人天天坐你对面不走，就是 obsession 痴迷执念。记：死坐在对面 = 着魔。

collocations: 近乎必然的事；高度肯定
sentence: We grow up craving certainty, as if life were a contract that guarantees outcomes. But the older I get, the more I suspect that certainty is a comfort we invent rather than a fact we discover. What matures in us is not the ability to predict everything, but the calm to act well without it—choosing, committing, and correcting course while the ground keeps shifting beneath our feet.
sentence_zh: 我们从小渴望确定，仿佛人生是一份保证结果的契约。可年纪越大，我越怀疑确定性不过是我们自己发明的一种安慰，而非被发现的真相。真正成熟起来的，并不是预知一切的能力，而是在没有确定的情况下依然从容行事的定力——边选择、边投入、边修正方向，任凭脚下的地面不断变动。
mnemonic: certainty = cert（确定，同 certain）+ -tain？不：是 certain + -ty 名词后缀。certain 里藏 cert『确信』，加 -ty 变抽象名词：certain（确定的）→ certainty（确定性）。记：cert 三兄弟 certain/sure/certainty 都含 cert=铁板钉钉。

sentence: Long before results become visible, patient people quietly cultivate the conditions in which growth can happen. A writer cultivates attention by reading slowly; a farmer cultivates soil by resting it; a leader cultivates trust by keeping small promises. Nothing dramatic occurs on any given day, yet over years the difference between those who cultivate and those who merely wait becomes impossible to ignore.
sentence_zh: 早在成果显现之前，有耐心的人就已默默培育着让成长得以发生的条件。写作者通过缓慢阅读培养专注，农夫通过休耕养护土地，领导者通过兑现小承诺积累信任。任何单独一天都看不出什么惊人变化，但多年之后，懂得培育的人与只会等待的人之间的差距，已再也无法忽视。
mnemonic: cultivate = cult(耕种，和culture同根，文化也是『耕』出来的) + ivate → 在地里耕种，就是培养庄稼；在人身上耕，就是培养人才。记住：culture文化、cultivate培养，都是同一把『锄头』刨出来的。

zh: 奢侈，豪华；奢侈品；豪华的
sentence: We tend to treat solitude as a luxury, something to be earned after the real work of the day is done. But perhaps that framing is backwards: attention, rest, and unhurried thought are not indulgences for the idle few, they are the raw material of a considered life. When we finally allow ourselves the luxury of boredom, we often discover the ideas we had been too busy to notice.
sentence_zh: 我们往往把独处当作一种奢侈，仿佛要等一天真正的工作做完之后才有资格享受。但也许这种想法恰恰颠倒了：专注、休息和不慌不忙的思考，并非闲人的放纵，而是过一种经过深思的生活的原料。当我们终于允许自己享受无聊这份奢侈时，常常会发现自己一直忙得无暇注意的那些想法。
mnemonic: luxury = lux（光）+ ury：古罗马『lux』就是光，有钱人家里灯烛通明、金碧辉煌，全是光的堆砌，这就是奢侈品/奢华。记住：能挥霍『光』的，就是 luxury。

zh: 实现；领悟，恍然大悟；变卖（资产）
sentence: Growth rarely announces itself with fireworks; more often it arrives as a quiet realization, waiting for us on an ordinary Tuesday. For years I believed success meant outpacing everyone around me, until the realization came that I had been racing strangers while neglecting the people who actually knew my name. Since then, I have measured my days differently, treating each small realization of what truly matters as progress worth celebrating.
sentence_zh: 成长很少伴随着烟花宣告它的到来；更多时候，它以一次安静的领悟抵达，在某个平平常常的星期二等着我们。多年来我一直以为成功意味着跑赢身边的每一个人，直到我意识到，自己一直在和陌生人赛跑，却冷落了那些真正记得我名字的人。从那以后，我换了一种方式衡量自己的日子，把每一次对何为重要的领悟，都当作值得庆祝的进展。
mnemonic: real（真实的）+ ize（动词后缀：使…化）→ 使真实化：把想法「变成现实」就是实现；而当真相突然「变得真实」砸到你眼前，就是你「意识到」了。记：real到底 = 实现；real 到心头 = 意识到。

sentence: There is a quiet dignity in owning fewer things, in letting go rather than accumulating. When we no longer have endless resources at our disposal, we begin to weigh what truly matters, and the discipline of that weighing shapes character. Even the disposal of old belongings becomes a small ritual of reflection, a way of deciding who we are becoming.
sentence_zh: 拥有更少的东西，学会放手而非不断积攒，其中自有一种安静的尊严。当我们不再拥有取之不尽的资源可供支配时，我们便开始掂量什么才是真正重要的，而这种掂量的纪律塑造了品格。即使是清理旧物，也成了一种小小的反思仪式，一种决定我们正在成为什么样的人的方式。
mnemonic: dis（分开）+ pos（放，同position）+ al（名词尾）→ 把东西分开放出去任人安排 → 处置权；at one's disposal = 东西都摊开放在你面前，任你支配。记住：dis-pos，'放'出去就是处置。

sentence: Somewhere along the way, I stopped treating every setback as a verdict and started treating it as information. If a plan failed, I asked what the failure revealed, adjusted accordingly, and moved on without much ceremony. That shift sounds small, but it changed how I work: less energy spent defending my ego, more spent reading the situation and responding to what is actually there.
sentence_zh: 不知从什么时候起，我不再把每一次挫折当作判决，而是把它当作信息。如果一个计划失败了，我会问这次失败揭示了什么，据此做出调整，然后不动声色地继续前行。这种转变听起来微不足道，却改变了我工作的方式：花在维护自尊上的精力少了，花在观察形势、对真实存在的情况作出回应上的精力多了。
mnemonic: accordingly = ac + cord + ing + ly。cord 是「心」(同 cardiac 心脏的)，ac 向外。两颗心对上号 = accord 一致。加上 -ly 就是「照着一致的那样办」→ 因此、相应地。钩子：cord 是心，心对上了，办事才有依据。

sentence: By the time she turned forty, she understood that a declaration, whether of independence or of love, is less a moment than a threshold. You say the words, and then the real work begins. Her resignation letter was only a declaration of intent; what followed were the quiet, unglamorous years of building the life she had claimed.
sentence_zh: 到四十岁时，她终于明白，宣言——无论是独立的宣言还是爱的表白——与其说是一个瞬间，不如说是一道门槛。话说出口，真正的工作才刚刚开始。她的辞职信不过是一份意向声明；随后的，是默默无闻、毫不光鲜的岁月，去建造她所宣告的那种生活。
mnemonic: declaration = de（完全）+ clar（clear，清楚）+ ation（名词后缀）→ 把话完全说清楚 = 郑重宣告。独立宣言 Declaration of Independence 就是把立场「讲清楚」给全世界听。记法：clar 看见 clarity（清晰）就想起——说清楚了，就是宣言。

sentence: There comes a point in every long project when the initial excitement has worn thin and the work feels mechanical. What we need then is not more discipline but something fresh: a colleague who can inject new life into the routine, a small change of method, even a day away. The best teams know how to inject energy deliberately, rather than waiting for it to return on its own.
sentence_zh: 每个漫长的项目都会走到这样一个节点：最初的兴奋已经淡去，工作变得机械。这时我们需要的不是更多的自律，而是某种新鲜感：一位能为日常注入新活力的同事，一个方法上的小小改变，甚至是外出的一天。最好的团队懂得刻意地注入能量，而不是被动地等它自己回来。
mnemonic: in（往里）+ ject（投、扔，同 eject 往外扔、project 往前投）→ 往里扔 = 注入。医生把药水「往里扔」进血管，就是注射。ject 就是「扔」：eject 扔出去，inject 扔进来，方向一反意思就清楚。

sentence: Somewhere between micromanagement and neglect lies the quiet art of knowing when to supervise. A good mentor watches without hovering, steps in before small mistakes become large ones, and trusts enough to let people find their own way. I have come to believe that the best leaders supervise less than they seem to, yet notice more than anyone realizes, offering guidance only when it truly matters.
sentence_zh: 在事无巨细的管控与放任不管之间，存在着一种安静的艺术——懂得何时该监督。好的导师看着却不过度干预，在小错误演变成大问题之前介入，又足够信任，让人走出自己的路。我渐渐相信，最好的领导者监督得比看上去少，却比任何人察觉到的都多，只在真正重要的时候才给予指导。
mnemonic: super 在上 + vis 看：领导站在「上面」往下「看」你干活，就是在监督你。就像 viser 的 vis（如 vision 视觉），上面那双眼睛一直盯着——super 在上 + vis 看 = 在上面盯着看 = 监督。

zh: 先于……发生（或出现）；走在……前面；优于
collocations: a brief introduction precedes the talk
sentence: Every achievement is quietly preceded by a long stretch of unglamorous work, yet we tend to remember only the moment of success. The failures that preceded it rarely make it into the story we tell, which is a pity, because they contain most of the learning. If we honored the slow years that precede any visible progress, we might be more patient with ourselves now.
sentence_zh: 每一项成就之前，都悄然隔着一段漫长而不起眼的努力，可我们往往只记得成功的那个瞬间。先于成功出现的那些失败，很少会进入我们讲述的故事，这实在可惜，因为它们包含了大部分的收获。如果我们能珍视任何看得见的进步之前那些缓慢的岁月，或许此刻就能对自己多一些耐心。
mnemonic: pre（提前）+ cede（走，同 proceed 的 ceed）→ 走在前面 = precede。想想开幕式：领导 precede 入场，先走一步。cede=走，pre=先，先走的就是『在……之前』。

zh: 盾牌；保护者；防护物；保护，遮蔽，屏蔽
forms: 动词过去式 / 过去分词
collocations: shield one's eyes from the light
sentence: As we grow older, we begin to see that the people we once resented for shielding us were often the ones bearing the blows themselves. A parent's caution, a mentor's bluntness, a friend's silence—each is a kind of shield, imperfect and sometimes suffocating, yet raised against a world they understood better than we did. Gratitude often arrives only after the shield is quietly lowered.
sentence_zh: 随着年龄增长，我们渐渐明白，那些曾因保护我们而被我们埋怨的人，往往才是真正承受打击的人。父母的谨慎、导师的直言、朋友的沉默——每一种都是一面盾牌，并不完美，有时甚至令人窒息，却是他们为了替我们挡住那个他们比我们更了解的世界而举起的。而感激，常常要等到盾牌悄然放下之后才会到来。
mnemonic: shield 谐音“希尔盾”：游戏角色希尔举起一面大盾，替全队挡下攻击——举“盾”护身就是 shield。一个音节直接炸出“盾牌/保护”的画面。

zh: 志向，抱负；渴望；（医学）吸入
sentence: For years I mistook ambition for aspiration, chasing titles and salaries that left me oddly hollow. It was only after a long, quiet winter that I understood the difference: ambition looks outward, comparing, while aspiration looks inward, asking what kind of person I genuinely wish to become. That shift did not make the work easier, but it made every ordinary morning feel like part of something worth building.
sentence_zh: 多年来我一直把野心错当抱负，追逐头衔与薪水，内心却莫名空虚。直到度过一个漫长而安静的冬天，我才明白二者的区别：野心向外张望，忙于比较；抱负向内审视，追问自己究竟想成为怎样的人。这一转变并没有让工作变轻松，却让每一个平凡的清晨都像是某种值得建造之物的一部分。
mnemonic: aspiration = a(加强) + spir(呼吸) + ation(名词)。同根词 respire(呼吸)、inspire(吸气→激励)。渴望就是把胸中那口气用力往上「呼」向高处—— aspiring 的那种向上的气息，就是渴望、抱负。记逻辑：一口气往上顶 = 心往高处想。

sentence: Every choice we make quietly sets a precedent, whether we notice it or not. The first time a manager excuses a missed deadline, or a friend accepts an empty apology, a pattern is born that others will follow. Breaking with precedent takes courage, precisely because it means admitting that the standard we once established was wrong all along.
sentence_zh: 我们做出的每一个选择都在悄悄开创先例，无论我们是否察觉。当管理者第一次原谅一个错过的截止日期，或朋友接受一次空洞的道歉时，一种他人将沿袭的模式就此诞生。打破先例需要勇气，恰恰因为这意味着承认我们曾确立的标准从一开始就是错的。
mnemonic: precedent = pre(在前) + ced(走，同 proceed 的 ced) + ent(人/物)：走在前面的人踩出的路。他先走了，后来者照着走——这就是「先例」。判案讲 precedent，就是照前人走过的路判。

sentence: We spend so much of our working lives chasing deadlines that we forget how few of our achievements will feel truly eternal. Yet that realization is oddly liberating rather than bleak: if nothing lasts forever, then what matters is the quality of attention we bring to each ordinary day, the patience with which we treat colleagues, and the small, unglamorous acts of care that quietly outlive us.
sentence_zh: 我们把工作生涯中太多的时间花在追赶截止日期上，以至于忘了自己的成就里能有几个真正称得上永恒。然而这个认识非但不令人沮丧，反而有种奇特的解脱感：既然没有什么是永存的，那么真正要紧的，是我们对待每一个平凡日子的专注品质，是我们对待同事的耐心，还有那些不起眼、毫不张扬的关怀之举——它们会悄然比我们活得更久。
mnemonic: eternal = e（向外）+ tern（词根，转，同 turn）+ al：连时间之轮都转不动它，所以是永恒的。对比 internal（内部）同款后缀。记住逻辑：转不出去、停在那儿的，就是永恒。

collocations: 正面碰撞（常喻激烈冲突）
sentence: Working closely with ambitious people eventually reveals the fault lines beneath any shared goal, and sooner or later a collision of interests seems inevitable. But I have come to see these collisions less as disasters and more as moments of clarification: they force everyone to state plainly what they actually want. A team that survives one honest collision often emerges more resilient, its agreements finally anchored in truth rather than politeness.
sentence_zh: 与雄心勃勃的人共事久了，终究会暴露出任何共同目标之下的裂痕，利益冲突的碰撞迟早难以避免。但我渐渐不再把这些冲突视为灾难，而是当作澄清真相的时刻：它们迫使每个人坦诚说出自己真正想要什么。一个挺过一次真诚碰撞的团队，往往变得更有韧性，彼此的共识也终于建立在真实而非客套之上。
mnemonic: col（一起）+ lis（撞，同 slide 滑）+ ion → 两车一起滑过来撞上 = 碰撞。记：两个一起滑，必然撞。

sentence: In an age when misinformation travels faster than correction, the habit of pausing to verify what we read has become a quiet form of intellectual discipline. Before forwarding a shocking headline or repeating a friend's confident assertion, we might ask whether anyone has actually verified it. That small delay between reaction and reflection is where genuine critical thinking begins, and where honest people distinguish themselves from careless ones.
sentence_zh: 在错误信息比更正传播得更快的时代，养成暂停下来核实所读内容的习惯，已成为一种静默的智识修养。在转发一条耸动的标题或重复朋友笃定的断言之前，我们不妨问问自己：是否真的有人核实过它？反应与反思之间的这段小小延迟，正是真正的批判性思维的起点，也是诚实的人与草率的人分野之处。
mnemonic: verify = ver（真，同 very 的本义「真实」）+ ify（使…化）→「使变真」，即核实真假。记住：very 不是「很」，本义是「真」，verify 就是把事情验真。

sentence: Every organization large enough to matter eventually breeds a faction: a cluster of people who feel unheard and begin to bargain as a bloc. It is tempting to condemn such splits as disloyalty, but often they are the honest symptom of grievances that polite consensus had buried. Leaders who listen early may dissolve the faction; leaders who suppress it usually guarantee that the fracture reappears, harder and angrier, at the worst possible moment.
sentence_zh: 任何一个足够重要的组织，最终都会滋生出一个派系：一群感到自己不被倾听的人，开始以集体的方式讨价还价。人们很容易把这种分裂斥为不忠，但它往往只是被体面的共识所掩埋的不满的诚实症状。早早倾听的领导者也许能化解派系；而压制它的领导者，通常只会保证裂痕在最糟糕的时刻再度出现，且更坚硬、更愤怒。
mnemonic: fact 做 + ion 名词后缀：一群人一起“做事”抱成团，就是派系。fact 也可理解为“共同的主张/事实”——公司里主张同一套 fact 的人凑成一伙，就成了 faction 派系。一个词里藏着 fact，说明派系成员都自认握着‘事实’。

sentence: There is an immense difference between being busy and being truly productive. For years I filled my days with small tasks, mistaking motion for progress. Only when I stepped back did I see how much energy I had poured into work that mattered little. Growth, I have learned, demands that we measure not the quantity of our effort but the weight of what we choose to carry.
sentence_zh: 忙碌与真正的高效之间存在着巨大的差别。多年来，我用琐事填满每一天，把忙碌误当作前进。直到退后一步，我才看清自己把多少精力倾注在了无关紧要的事情上。我逐渐明白，成长要求我们衡量的不是付出的数量，而是我们所选择承担之事的分量。
mnemonic: im（不）+ mense（测量，同 measure）→ 大到「没法测量」→ 巨大的。浩瀚星空 immense，因为尺子根本量不过来。记：量不了的就是 immense。

zh: 起重要作用的；作为手段的；乐器的
collocations: 对做成某事起关键作用
sentence: Looking back on my first year at the company, I realize how much depended on people who never sought credit. A senior editor was instrumental in helping me shape my scattered drafts into something publishable, and she did it quietly, without ceremony. Success, I have come to believe, is rarely a solo performance; it is an arrangement in which the most essential players are often the least visible.
sentence_zh: 回顾我在公司的第一年，我才意识到有多少成果离不开那些从不邀功的人。一位资深编辑在帮助我把零散的草稿打磨成可发表的文字方面起了关键作用，而且她做得很安静，毫不张扬。我渐渐相信，成功很少是独奏；它更像一场合奏，其中最不可或缺的乐手往往最不显眼。
mnemonic: instrument 是工具、器械，-al 表示“像…的”。起作用的不是人，而是“工具”——像一件得力器械那样帮忙，所以是“起关键作用的”：Music was instrumental in his success. 记住：像工具一样有用 = 有帮助的。

zh: 失去知觉的；未察觉的；无意识的
sentence: Much of what drives us lies beneath awareness: we act, choose, and react while unconscious of the habits quietly steering us. Recognising this is uncomfortable but liberating. A manager who admits her unconscious bias toward confident speakers may finally hear the quiet colleague with the better idea. Growth begins not with grand resolutions, but with the slow, honest work of making the invisible visible.
sentence_zh: 驱动我们的许多东西都藏于觉知之下：我们在并未意识到那些习惯正悄悄引导自己的情况下行动、选择、做出反应。承认这一点令人不安，却也是种解放。一位管理者若承认自己对自信健谈者怀有无意识的偏爱，也许终于能听见那位安静同事更好的想法。成长并非始于宏大的决心，而是始于把不可见之物变得可见的、缓慢而诚实的工作。
mnemonic: 拆开记：un（不）+ con（共同）+ sc（知道，同 science 的词根 sci=知道）+ ious。全宇宙都“不知道”→ 失去知觉的、无意识的。比如他被打晕后 unconscious，就是“什么也不知道了”。记住：sc=知道，前面加 un 就是不知道。

zh: 转移（注意力、资金等）；使转向；使消遣
sentence: It is easy to let an urgent email divert our attention from the work that actually matters. I have watched entire weeks slip away this way, energy diverted to whatever shouts loudest rather than whatever runs deepest. Perhaps growth begins the moment we notice the drift and quietly redirect ourselves, not with drama, but with the patient discipline of returning, again and again, to what we truly intend.
sentence_zh: 一封紧急的邮件很容易让我们把注意力从真正重要的工作上转移开。我曾眼睁睁看着整整几周就这样溜走，精力被转向喊得最响的事情，而非最深沉的事情。也许成长恰恰始于我们察觉到这种漂移并悄悄调整方向的那一刻——不是轰轰烈烈，而是怀着耐心的自律，一次又一次地回到自己真正想要的东西上。
mnemonic: divert = di（=dis，离开）+ vert（转），把方向『转走』。堵车时警察挥手让车流改道，就是 divert。vert 你早认识：vertical 竖直、convert 转换——全是『转』。记住：di = 转离 → 使转向、转移注意力。

sentence: What separates a good colleague from a great one is rarely talent alone; it is the habit of being thoughtful. A thoughtful person notices the small things—someone working late, a friend gone quiet—and responds with care rather than speed. Over the years I have learned that thoughtful decisions, though slower to make, tend to age far better than clever ones.
sentence_zh: 把好同事和优秀同事区分开来的，很少是天赋本身，而是那种体贴周到的习惯。一个体贴的人会注意到细微之处——有人加班到深夜，朋友忽然沉默——并以关怀而非匆忙作出回应。这些年我逐渐明白，深思熟虑的决定虽然做得慢，却往往比聪明的决定经得起时间的考验。
mnemonic: thought（想）+ ful（充满）→ 脑子里总装着别人：吃饭前先想你不吃辣，下雨天记得你没带伞。一句话：满脑子都在想 = 体贴周到的。

zh: 被动的；消极的；（语法）被动语态
sentence: For years I took a passive attitude toward my own career, waiting for opportunities to arrive rather than chasing them. It felt safer to be the one who was chosen than the one who chose. But growth, I eventually realized, rarely rewards the passive observer; it belongs to those who risk an opinion, make an awkward request, and accept that a life shaped by others will never quite feel like their own.
sentence_zh: 多年来，我对自己的职业抱着一种消极的态度，等着机会找上门，而不是主动去争取。做一个被挑选的人，似乎比做挑选的人更安全。但我最终明白，成长很少眷顾被动的旁观者；它属于那些敢于表达观点、敢于提出笨拙请求、并接受“由他人塑造的人生永远不会真正属于自己”这一事实的人。
mnemonic: pass 词根=承受（如 passion 原意“忍受之苦”），-ive 形容词后缀 → 只能“承受、不去动”的 = 被动的。想想 passive smoking（被动吸烟）：你没点烟，烟却 pass 到你身上，只能默默承受，这就是被动。

sentence: In any workplace, there eventually comes a moment when silence costs more than speech. When a colleague is treated unfairly, what we feel is not mere annoyance but genuine outrage, and that feeling deserves respect. Yet outrage, left unspoken, curdles into bitterness; expressed thoughtfully, it can correct a wrong and even strengthen trust. Learning to voice it well may be one of the quiet markers of professional maturity.
sentence_zh: 在任何职场里，迟早都会出现这样一个时刻：沉默的代价超过了开口。当同事受到不公对待时，我们感受到的不只是恼火，而是真正的义愤，这种情绪值得被尊重。然而，义愤若憋在心里不说，会发酵成怨怼；若表达得当，却能纠正错误，甚至加深信任。学会恰当地表达愤怒，或许正是职业成熟度的一个隐性标志。
mnemonic: out（冲出来）+ rage（暴怒）→ 怒气冲到外面来了，超出正常愤怒，就成了「暴行、义愤」。想象有人气得直接掀桌冲出门：outrage！记住：怒气冲出 = outrageous 骇人的。
